Phoenix Wing Academy.text:
Phoenix Wing Academy trains mages for public defense, security readiness, and the practical work of keeping people safe when danger is real. Its red uniforms and phoenix heraldry accompany demanding drills, a fierce dueling culture, monster fieldcraft, and preparation for protecting others under pressure. Lessons connect combat execution with judgment: identify the threat, control the scene, coordinate with others, and know when to stop. Students receive broad magical education comparable to the other academies; no element, temperament, or moral alignment determines admission.
Akane Todo represents Phoenix Wing Academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Kōhei Sanada manages its academic system and daily operations. Its public assignments can include authorized protection, threat assessment, dungeon reconnaissance, and supervised monster tracking or subdual. Student status grants no independent power to arrest, sentence, seize property, or act as a professional soldier. The City Guard handles ordinary policing, the Magistrate's Hall handles judgments, and the Elite Strikeforce retains its separate exceptional duties.
Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region under authorization from the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. Readiness is tested in the field as well as the arena. The institution's demanding reputation contains ambitious duelists, reluctant fighters, practical researchers, cooks, and people who disagree about what responsible defense requires.

Hydra Head Academy.text:
Hydra Head Academy prepares mages to work across people, institutions, and places: diplomacy, trade, logistics, community assistance, mediation, and the coordination that makes civic projects function. Violet clothing and hydra heraldry identify an academy where an impressive result is often one that several parties can actually carry out. Teaching joins magical competence with negotiation, preparation, supplies, routes, and the consequences of conflicting interests. Its broad curriculum and combat instruction remain comparable to the other academies.
Reika Saionji represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Kiyoko Fujinami runs daily academic operations in close partnership with Reika Saionji. Advice, commissions, research collaborations, and authorized civic assistance connect the school to the city. Supporting a dispute does not confer judicial authority; facilitating trade does not establish ownership of another person's goods. Courts and civic offices retain their actual responsibilities.
Every student must complete a Great Sage- or court-authorized expedition outside the Glowhaven region. A field assignment may turn on cooperation, transport, community needs, a survey, or a dangerous situation requiring trained magic. Diplomatic emphasis does not make the academy defenseless or its people uniformly agreeable. Mercenary, shy, confrontational, gentle, extravagant, and intensely private people can all belong here.

Gryffin Tail Academy.text:
Gryffin Tail Academy advances magical knowledge through analytical study, field investigation, and the infrastructure needed to make findings useful. Cyan uniforms and gryffin heraldry accompany demanding academic standards, exact practical assessments, and the most advanced research facilities among Glowhaven's four academies. Its education still includes broad magical and combat training; an athlete, reluctant reader, socialite, or struggling practitioner is not misplaced simply because the institution values rigorous work.
Gryffin Tail Academy is the only academy with a formal specialization in magitech research: mechanical engineering integrated with magic, enchantments, or magical components. An enchanted necklace is not automatically magitech, and other academies and artisans remain able to make, buy, study, and repair enchanted goods. Its expeditions can survey dungeons, measure unusual environments, examine specimens and sites, and bring back evidence for further study. Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region authorized by the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court.
Gen'ichirō Mizuhara represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons; Norio Shibata manages its records and day-to-day academic administration as Headmaster. Research prestige can make a recommendation valuable and an unfair assessment damaging. Published standards, private ambition, practical results, and the treatment of inconvenient evidence can pull in different directions. A strict instructor's preferred incantation is not a universal law of spellcasting.

Dragon Hoard Academy.text:
Dragon Hoard Academy specializes in expeditionary exploration and work with relics: finding and surveying unfamiliar sites, assessing discoveries, and preparing for the difficult handling and return of objects whose significance or danger may not be immediately apparent. Yellow-and-gold clothing and dragon heraldry accompany a formidable, exacting institutional tradition. Its strictness descends chiefly from its founder's character and generations of teaching practice; it is not a personality shared by every student or a single-word creed.
Tōru Shizunami represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Miyu Asahina keeps its academic programs and daily operations working. Genzō Iwakura's fieldcraft, Madoka Narukami's demanding practical instruction, Noriaki Takatsuki's exact preparation, and the existing Discovery Labs, Observatory, Exhibition Hall, and Training Court support a school that expects discoveries to survive the journey home. Exploration and relic work complement its broad magical education and combat training rather than replacing them.
Every student must complete an expedition outside the Glowhaven region under authorization from the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. Relic-oriented missions may involve survey, identification, careful documentation, stabilization, or an explicitly permitted recovery. Discovery grants no automatic title to an object, private site, or another community's heritage. Permissions, safety, custody, and actual claims matter; no universal salvage law is presumed. Curious students, stern professionals, gamblers, repairers, reluctant participants, and a famously talented Archon who dislikes unnecessary work retain their own priorities.

Conclave of Archons.text:
The Conclave of Archons brings together the four exceptionally capable mages who publicly represent Glowhaven's academies: Akane Todo of Phoenix Wing Academy, Gen'ichirō Mizuhara of Gryffin Tail Academy, Tōru Shizunami of Dragon Hoard Academy, and Reika Saionji of Hydra Head Academy. Each holds their academy's seat. The Conclave gives the institutions an arena for negotiation, coordinated responses, research interests, and rivalry. The headmasters continue managing their respective schools.

The Conclave is distinct from the larger Council that elects the Great Sage. It carries influence without making its four members the only eligible candidates. Public representation and exceptional capability do not mean the Archons administer every street, shop, or classroom themselves. Routine inquiries go to the appropriate local office; an Archon appears when their actual responsibilities or interests warrant it.

The Council.text:
The Council is Glowhaven City's larger governing body and the institution that elects the Great Sage. It is separate from the four-member Conclave of Archons. A candidate may be an Archon, a council member, or someone from outside either group whose ability earns sufficient support. A term lasts up to one hundred years or ends at the incumbent's death; reelection is possible.

The Council has elected Ilyra Stillglass three times over her 254-year rule because it has continued to regard her as the best choice. Academy influence, noble households, infrastructure, and civic interests make its deliberations important to ordinary life. Petitions and proposals reach decisions through actual representatives, evidence, and negotiation. Wealth, sponsorship, or a school title can open a conversation without granting ownership of the Great Sage's office. The Council's authority does not turn every official into an omniscient enforcer.

The Elite Strikeforce.text:
The Elite Strikeforce serves the Great Sage as Glowhaven City's elite military and confidential security force. It handles major threats and sensitive operations beyond ordinary street policing. Its personnel can also carry the Great Sage's authority on diplomatic journeys to neighboring nations, where judgment and discretion can matter as much as destructive power.

The force operates separately from the City Guard. An ordinary theft report, classroom dispute, or rude visitor does not normally demand its intervention. Serious evidence of a major threat can bring specialized personnel, actual orders, and coordinated action. Its public reputation rests on exceptional capability and proximity to the Great Sage, while identities, assignments, and operational details need not be public knowledge.

Academy Leadership.text:
Academy leadership in Glowhaven separates the Archon's representative office from the headmaster's administrative role. The Archon is an exceptionally powerful and capable mage who represents the institution publicly and holds its seat on the Conclave of Archons. Archons have earned substantial respect through their accomplishments, with their individual strengths extending beyond a single measure of dueling power.

The headmaster manages the school system and day-to-day operations, including the practical coordination that keeps teaching and institutional work functioning. Archons appoint headmasters they trust to advance their goals. Their working relationships differ, and the distinction between the offices allows leadership, administration, research, and public duties to be shared rather than concentrated in one person's schedule.

Magic Learning and Affinity.text:
Magic learning in Glowhaven distinguishes natural affinity from learned competence. All elements and schools of magic can be learned by anyone; an affinity makes its associated spells more intuitive and easier to learn. Many residents remain with a familiar affinity because it is convenient and sufficient for their work.

Learning outside an affinity is often awkward at first. A student must become accustomed to unfamiliar magical patterns and habits, but continued practice can make that casting comfortable and dependable. Serious mages study several elements alongside theory, and the academies include work beyond a student's natural affinity in their education. Affinity does not set an exclusive spell list, determine a person's occupation, or guarantee great power. A practiced specialist, a capable generalist, and an inexperienced mage with a rare affinity can have very different strengths.

Soul-bearing learners circulate internal mana through practiced blueprints, using the body or a suitable catalyst. Affinity, reservoir size, learned control, and equipment assistance are distinct. A trained practitioner can learn bodily Enchantment or another school outside their natural affinity. Personalized speech and gestures are aids rather than universal gates to casting.

Ice developed historically from Water, Metal from Earth and Sound from Wind, but they can now be studied independently. Space remains an advanced study requiring Gravity; Time requires exceptional Space and Spellcraft preparation and an actual rare teaching route. Time affinity is excluded for everyone, including oracles. Magitech and Spellcraft are technical skills, not affinity choices. Temporary conjuration and lasting work on existing matter are distinct.

The Evertree.text:
The Evertree is the great tree at the heart of Glowhaven City whose presence thickens the currents of mana in the surrounding air and environment. The denser mana is easier to sense and control; learners can sometimes almost feel its movement physically, giving practice a tangible quality that is harder to find elsewhere.

This environment attracts people interested in magic's study, practical use, and refinement. Apprentices can better recognize the shape of a spell, experienced mages can examine subtler effects, and craftspeople can work in a place where careful magical adjustments are easier to perceive. Progress still requires training and judgment, but the Evertree makes Glowhaven an unusually favorable place to develop them. Ilyra Stillglass tends its magical weave as part of the Great Sage's responsibilities. The landmark's name is always the Evertree.

Its locally dense ambient mana aids sensing, control, and learning; it is not established as the origin of every mana source or a substitute for finite personal capacity.

The Great Sage and Succession.text:
The Great Sage is Glowhaven City's elected ruler, treated locally with the authority and ceremony of a king or queen. The office combines civic leadership with stewardship of the Evertree's magical weave. A large governing council elects the incumbent; eligibility is open beyond the four Archons and beyond council membership.

A term lasts until the incumbent's death or up to one hundred years, with reelection possible. Ilyra Stillglass, also known as the White Lotus, has governed for 254 years across three terms after being reelected twice. Her long tenure has made her leadership a familiar constant across generations. The academies are already maneuvering around the approaching succession, each hoping to influence the next choice. Ilyra Stillglass's academy of origin remains unknown; her established authority rests on the council's repeated selection rather than an attributed school allegiance.

Elvish Language.text:
Elvish is represented as French in Glowhaven's story text and dialogue. When a character speaks Elvish, render their spoken words in French rather than inventing another language. Characters may speak the city's common language as well as Elvish, and an individual's fluency depends on their background.

At least one Elvish nation exists beyond Glowhaven City. Its name and fuller political and cultural details remain to be developed. A foreign speaker's use of Elvish can express familiarity, privacy, frustration, or affection without implying that every listener understands it. Understanding should follow what the scene establishes about a listener rather than automatically spreading to the whole cast.

Glowhaven City and Its People.text:
Glowhaven City is a flourishing center of magical life, education, and craftsmanship whose prosperity rests on the Evertree and the people drawn to it. Residents include established local families, working craftspeople, merchants, farmers bringing goods to market, ambitious students, researchers, and visitors seeking tools or instruction they cannot easily find at home.

Magic is woven into ordinary life, but the city also runs on meals, deliveries, repairs, wages, paperwork, and personal relationships. An accomplished mage may be a poor administrator, an excellent shopkeeper may know only a few practical spells, and a celebrated duelist still needs someone to make their boots. Glowhaven's extraordinary magical resources support a recognizable society full of pride, affection, ambition, inconvenience, and daily work.

The Founding of Glowhaven.text:
Glowhaven City's founding is associated with four great Archmages whose followers later established Phoenix Wing Academy, Hydra Head Academy, Gryffin Tail Academy, and Dragon Hoard Academy around their respective teachings. Local legend holds that the four founders planted the Evertree together, making its cultivation an enduring image of the city's origins. The planting story is a founding legend rather than a fully documented account of the Evertree's nature.

The four founders remain part of civic memory. The monument at Four Sages Bazaar connects busy present-day commerce with the city's beginnings, while the academies preserve different interpretations of their legacies. Local accounts disagree on the planting's exact circumstances; the shared monument remains a civic meeting point rather than proof of every retelling.

Magic in Everyday Life.text:
Magic in everyday Glowhaven is commonplace and usually modest. Many residents know a small repertoire of cantrips for tasks such as producing light, starting a cooking flame, rinsing tools, guiding a little water, or moving a small object. What someone actually knows reflects their affinity, upbringing, occupation, interest, and practice.

A household may rely on a few familiar tricks for years, while a shop worker learns the spells most useful at the counter or bench. Ordinary magical competence is different from the broad study and sustained practice of a serious mage. Small conveniences sit beside mundane work: food still needs preparing, streets need maintaining, tools wear out, and a spell only helps when someone understands the task. Familiarity also produces ordinary irritation, from an unreliable charm to a neighbor whose decorative magic is far too bright.

Body casting is a normal starting method: a cooking flame on a finger or a small light need not require a purchased focus. Ordinary pets cannot deliberately cast merely because the city is rich in mana. Practical household magic is learned execution of familiar blueprints, not evidence that everyone can invent Freeform workings on demand.

Magic, Training, and Practical Limits.text:
Practical magic in Glowhaven rewards understanding, repetition, and control. Dense environmental mana makes learning easier, while useful results still depend on the caster's preparation, concentration, and experience. Large effects require more effort and present greater difficulties than familiar cantrips.

Skilled magic solves particular problems rather than replacing every profession at once. Maintaining a structure, organizing a food supply, treating an injury, crafting a reliable enchantment, and administering a district each require their own knowledge. Magical talent also varies within professions: a careful artisan need not be a celebrated fighter, and years of combat experience do not automatically teach civic management. Power has substantial value in emergencies, while ordinary development depends on many people applying different kinds of expertise.

Internal capacity has a partly inherited starting point and can grow through use. Ambient uptake varies with conditions, and calm rest restores usable mana more efficiently. At zero usable mana a caster remains conscious; ordinary spells normally fizzle, with only a very difficult exceptional last-cast check offering a rare possibility. Ordinary casting never consumes soul-sustaining mana. Intentional physical augmentation belongs to Enchantment, while Arcane wards can protect the body. No routine humanoid soul-draining technique or solved clinical mana transfusion is established.

City Guard.text:
The City Guard patrols Glowhaven's streets and gates, investigates ordinary crimes, protects the public, and makes arrests within civic authority. Reports go through its headquarters and local officers; the Magistrate's Hall handles hearings and judgments. Tetsuya Ōmi is an established contact at headquarters, while officers at the gates have their own posts and immediate knowledge.

Guards are trained adults who use observation, practical magic, equipment, and coordinated tactics. They ask for support when a danger exceeds their strength and distinguish a witness's allegation from an established finding. Theft, assault, repeated violence, and murder can bring investigation, pursuit, actual capture, and a recorded custody order. Wraith Island provides the exterior approach to the separate Wraith Island Prison realm. Prisoners, authorized workers, visitors, and intruders have different permissions. The Elite Strikeforce has separate military and exceptional-security duties.

Civic Administration and Public Work.text:
Civic administration in Glowhaven depends on officials, clerks, planners, workers, and specialists carrying out continuing responsibilities beneath the Great Sage's authority. Petitions need reading, orders need communicating, supplies need arranging, public works need maintaining, and local disputes need people who can examine the facts.

Exceptional magical power does not provide the time or expertise to develop and administer an entire society alone. Most days involve ordinary work rather than a city-threatening attack. Influence therefore comes from access, experience, resources, and trusted service as well as combat strength. An attentive clerk, a reliable builder, or an experienced harbor worker can matter greatly to a problem that no spectacular spell would settle.

Noble Houses and Civic Development.text:
Noble houses in Glowhaven derive their standing from a mixture of recognized titles, land, accumulated wealth, family alliances, and service to the city and kingdom. The Great Sage's monarch-like authority includes the ability to reward service with formal honors and grants, including fiefs. Strategic marriages and inherited connections can strengthen a house's position over generations.

Many established houses have substantial ties to infrastructure and development: estates, agricultural production, trade facilities, workshops, roads, and other long-term undertakings can support both their wealth and their public importance. Their interests may align with civic prosperity or compete over resources, credit, and influence. Noble status creates expectations and advantages, while individual conduct ranges from conscientious service to arrogance and self-interest. The full title hierarchy and the responsibilities attached to particular grants remain undesigned.

Diplomacy and the Wider Kingdom.text:
Glowhaven is substantially self-governing, with the Great Sage exercising central local authority. Its noble households, court, and commercial institutions also participate in a wider kingdom through trade, obligations, and representation.

The Great Sage can send elite personnel abroad when credibility, discretion, and protection matter together. Visiting scholars, sailors, merchants, and foreign residents bring other customs. At least one Elvish nation exists beyond Glowhaven; its people speak Elvish, represented as French in dialogue. Foreign origin does not make every visitor a diplomat.

The Four Academies and Civic Service.text:
Glowhaven's four academies are public institutions serving the city and wider kingdom through different mandates, operating traditions, research, trained graduates, and supervised work. Phoenix Wing emphasizes public defense and readiness; Hydra Head diplomacy, trade, logistics, and community coordination; Gryffin Tail research, dungeon surveys, and formal magitech specialization; Dragon Hoard exploration, relic assessment, and responsible field recovery. These functions complement rather than monopolize one another.
All provide broadly comparable magical education and combat training. Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region authorized by the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. A school mandate grants neither automatic public office nor an exception to courts, ownership, evidence, or actual access. Archons represent institutions and hold Conclave seats; headmasters manage the school systems.
Institutional habits come from history, teaching methods, responsibilities, and the people who sustain or challenge them. Colors, emblems, and a public specialty do not sort students by personality, morality, affinity, or social class.

Enchanted Goods and Glowhaven's Trade.text:
Enchanted goods are Glowhaven's most distinctive commercial strength. The city is known for quality enchanted items, magical accessories, and trinkets whose practical usefulness and careful manufacture attract buyers from elsewhere. The Evertree's dense mana environment supports the training and fine control that help this work flourish.

The trade includes useful everyday objects as well as expensive and elaborate pieces. A small convenience can be a successful product, while a specialized commission may bring together several kinds of expertise. Shops, independent makers, established businesses, and noble interests can all participate in this economy. Imports, exports, and visiting customers connect Glowhaven's workshops to the harbor and caravan routes, making magical craftsmanship central to the city's identity without making every resident an enchanter.

Craftsmanship, Ownership, and Repair.text:
Magical craftsmanship in Glowhaven involves the fitting of an enchantment to an actual object, purpose, and user. Reliable work depends on materials, design, the maker's technique, and an understanding of how the item will be used. Dense local mana helps craftspeople examine their work closely, while good judgment and patient finishing still matter.

Enchanted objects also require ordinary ownership decisions: maintenance, repairs, replacement parts, appropriate handling, and help when something behaves unexpectedly. A useful trinket can last through regular use or become an expensive nuisance when neglected. Skilled repairers and suppliers therefore have their own place beside famous makers. Buying a magical item can lead to an ongoing relationship with a shop or craftsperson rather than ending the moment money changes hands.

Food, Farms, and Fisheries.text:
Glowhaven's food supply rests on extensive surrounding farmland, fishing through its harbor and coastal communities, and imports carried by established trade routes. Fields near settlements such as Brookmeadow produce food for the city, while markets connect growers, intermediaries, shops, kitchens, and households.

Magic assists useful parts of agricultural and domestic work, but provision still depends on cultivation, seasonal labor, storage, transport, and dependable trade. Fishing households, farmers, boat crews, port workers, and market sellers all contribute to meals that city residents can take for granted. Differences in quality, freshness, demand, and reliability give these relationships practical importance. An interruption can create local shortages, arguments, or extra work without becoming a kingdom-wide catastrophe.

Roads, Harbor, and Rural Communities.text:
Glowhaven's roads and Whitecrest Harbor connect the city to surrounding farms, villages, coastal settlements, islands, and more distant trade. The Caravan Outpost serves travelers on the western approaches, while gates and harbor facilities channel the regular movement of people and goods.

Nearby communities have lives and interests of their own. Residents visit the city for markets, services, work, equipment, or study, and city residents travel outward for supplies, family, business, and practical tasks. Journeys can carry gossip, friendships, disputes, and changes in fortune alongside cargo. Travel should respect the established map and actual approaches: a boat-linked settlement, a guarded gateway, and a wilderness path create different circumstances even when all appear within the same broad regional map.

Wealth and Neighborhood Life.text:
Neighborhood life in Glowhaven varies with resources, housing, work, and local expectations. The Cloud District's fine homes and proximity to the governing court create a different atmosphere from the working and middle-class lanes of Willowbend or the poorer settlements of East Greyfield and West Greyfield outside the walls.

Eastbloom Residences and Rosetimber Suburbs add their own forms of respectability, including notably strict residents' association rules. Differences in comfort and influence generate ambitions, resentments, friendships, and very petty disputes alongside serious concerns. Magical abundance coexists with uneven wealth because people still differ in property, opportunities, training, and connections. No fixed difference in Evertree access between these neighborhoods has been established.

Festivals and Everyday Sociability.text:
Glowhaven has many festivals and public celebrations, supported by a population that enjoys magical displays, food, commerce, and the chance to see and be seen. Market activity, performances, festive decorations, and gatherings can bring residents, visitors, workers, and students into the same streets. Specific festival names, dates, and a formal calendar remain to be designed.

Social life continues between large events in taverns, inns, teahouses, shops, residential lanes, and public places. The Crooked Tankard, the Golden Ladle, and the Jade Cup Teahouse offer different surroundings for ordinary conversation and recurring acquaintances. Humor can arise from personal pride, awkward invitations, incompatible habits, and local rules without every gathering becoming an emergency or involving the entire named cast.

The Eternal Crucible and Tournament Cult.text:
The Eternal Crucible is Glowhaven's great public arena, and its colosseum tournaments are among the city's largest events. Major contests draw spectators and participants into a shared spectacle where magical skill, tactical judgment, and memorable performances can become matters of public conversation.

Tournament occasions affect more than competitors. Visitors need food and lodging, craftspeople receive attention for equipment, merchants find customers, and residents develop favorites and rivalries. A skilled newcomer can gain recognition, while a famous competitor must live with expectations. Each event announces its entry conditions, format, schedule and prizes before registration. A spectator is not a registered competitor.

During an active tournament duel, competitors may not use mana potions or external stored-mana reserves from items. Ordinary control-assisting catalysts are not banned by that rule. Emergency mana-potion treatment is permitted once the match is officially stopped. Enforcement follows actual evidence and announced decisions; the rule supplies no omniscient detection or unannounced penalty.

Safety, Crime, and Dangerous Work.text:
Safety in Glowhaven is supported by guards, powerful protectors, public institutions, skilled residents, and ordinary cooperation. Most days are occupied by routine life rather than major monster attacks. Theft, fraud, personal disputes, damaged property, missing goods, and careless magic can still require investigation and practical assistance.

Power is valuable when force is needed, while many problems require evidence, time, local knowledge, or specialized judgment. Outside the city, travelers, workers, and monster hunters face circumstances shaped by terrain, distance, and the particular dangers of an area. The existence of exceptionally capable leaders leaves useful work for other people because protection, development, and daily administration are continuing shared responsibilities. A specific monster ecology and broader threat roster remain future lore.

An actual attempt to forcefully extract another being's internal mana is treated as attempted murder even if small. This does not establish that humanoids have a witnessed method, or that ordinary spell suppression is extraction. Investigation still needs evidence; studying a theory, possessing a rare affinity, and being accused are not convictions.

Greywatch Keep and the Founding Defenses.text:
Greywatch Keep is an obsolete outpost fort from the period when Glowhaven City was still being founded. Its position once served the needs of a younger settlement establishing its defenses and approaches. Those circumstances have changed, and the fort has no current official use.

Its weathered walls and disused rooms are evidence of the city's earlier scale rather than proof of a recent military disaster. The site can carry local memories, historical curiosity, and practical reminders of how far Glowhaven has developed. No current garrison, secret occupier, hidden treasure, or supernatural cause for its abandonment has been established.

Wraith Island Prison.text:
Wraith Island lies offshore from Glowhaven. Its prison is a secured stone campus with a landing, intake desk, records office, holding cells, a high-security block, supervised workshops, stores, an infirmary, visiting rooms, meal and exercise spaces, and a guarded sea wall. The exterior island shore is not unrestricted access to the prison.

The court sends people here under actual custody orders. Staff, approved contractors and visitors enter for their own duties and are not inmates. Short custodial terms can be served quietly or spent talking, exercising and taking suitable work. Release includes the return journey to Glowhaven. Other established cases and personal relationships remain real; an ended term does not make every witness forget.

Healing, Lasting Injury, and Age.text:
Healing magic in Glowhaven can be useful and powerful without making every physical condition reversible. The severity, nature, and history of an injury matter; some lasting damage remains difficult to remedy after the immediate wound has closed. Aging can also bring decline that ordinary magical treatment cannot meaningfully reverse.

A person can retain great magical knowledge or power while living with limited mobility, declining sight, fatigue, or a slow recovery. The availability of healing should therefore coexist with care, practical assistance, adaptation, and uncertainty. Individual medical details belong to the affected character's established information rather than being resolved automatically by the mere presence of a healer.

Healing mainly addresses physical injury. While applying it, a healer may feel and support mana circulation, without automatically refilling a reservoir or curing soul damage. Theoretical forced extraction below the usable threshold would cause unconscious mana shock; if survived, recovery could take weeks or months. Permanent damage is extremely rare and possible only after sudden, rapid shock. Mana replenishment alone does not cure that shock. No witnessed human extraction case is established.

Familiars and Everyday Companions.text:
Ordinary pets, bonded animal companions, mana beasts, and summoned manifestations are distinct. A bond does not give an ordinary soulless animal a circulating soul or spontaneous spells. Ordinary animals may contain inert mana and react to extreme ambient concentrations. Soul-bearing mana beasts can naturally employ magic; an arcane construct or temporary summoned form follows its actual summoning rather than assumed animal physiology.
Moonwhisker Emporium and other established services can help with appropriate care, equipment, advice, and handling. Feeding, supervision, temperament, and the owner's knowledge still matter. A magical companion need not be a secret revelation, and a mundane cat need not become a spellcaster. Individual bonds, costs, permissions, and creature abilities follow their actual records.

Glowhaven Marks and Everyday Prices.text:
Glowhaven accounts in marks. One Mark is one unit of spendable currency; quotes, wages, and debts use that same unit. Barter or a favor can replace money only when both sides agree. A quote, unpaid invoice, promised reward, and payment actually received are different things.

A plain meal costs about 2 marks, a substantial supper 4, a shared bunk 6, a plain private room 12 per night, and a packed lunch 3. Straightforward day labor pays about 18–25 marks and skilled work commonly 35–60. Quality, urgency, materials, access, and real risk can justify a stated difference. These anchors keep ordinary choices intelligible without requiring identical prices everywhere.

Repairs, Enchantment, and Commissions.text:
A basic inspection costs around 6 marks. A small repair normally costs 12–25 plus agreed parts. A simple focus starts near 60 marks and a dependable household enchanted lamp near 80; bespoke enchantments and durable combat equipment can cost hundreds or more. Price does not grant unlearned spells or prove workmanship.

A commission establishes purpose, materials, cost, deadline, and acceptance terms before work begins. Diagnosis, repair, replacement, ownership, and compensation remain separate decisions. Deposits and borrowed supplies are not wages. A completed job earns its agreed fee once, after the result is accepted.

Practical Work and Small Opportunities.text:
Workshops, shops, inns, farms, boats, and academies need deliveries, copying, stock checks, repairs, inspections, event setup, seasonal hands, and supervised research. A useful job identifies an actual contact and the result wanted. Beginners can contribute through care, skill, and observation without being the strongest mage present.

Clients can negotiate or refuse an estimate. Specialist or dangerous work pays differently from a small errand. Employment, a favor, and a shared meal do not create traveling-party membership. Repeat customers and reliable workers can gain trust, referrals, and opportunities through remembered conduct.

City Justice and Wraith Island Sentences.text:
The City Guard investigates and arrests; the Magistrate's Hall records hearings and judgments. Witnessed violence, murder, grave destruction, and repeated serious offenses can bring a coordinated response. Evidence, witnesses, actual resistance, and legal proceedings matter. Accusation or a failed persuasion attempt is not conviction.

Wraith Island Prison receives ordered serious custody and convicted offenders whose cases require offshore security. Records state the alleged or proven acts, legal status, belongings held, sentence or review, and appeal or release route. Serving time, authorized work, and escape are possible experiences. Escape can end physical captivity while leaving warrants, restitution, and remembered harm unresolved.

Prison Life, Work, and Access.text:
Wraith Island Prison is a secured physical island campus reached through controlled transport, with its own map of intake, cells, workshops, medical care and security. Shūgo Katase oversees daily custody operations. Chisato Kurebayashi handles intake and release; Ena Minamori runs the infirmary. Akira Oritsu supervises assigned work and escorts. Mirei Shiozaki operates authorized boats from Skullshore Landing.

Prisoners, employees and visitors have different permissions. A worker’s assignment does not open every gate, and a visitor is not an inmate. Inmates can talk, exercise, accept suitable work or simply serve their term. Staff explain the option of spending uneventful time quietly. Short custodial terms end with release and transport back to Glowhaven; a work shift or a knockout does not by itself discharge a prisoner.

Actual treatment, injuries, relationships and personal belongings remain part of a person’s life. A lawful release is a return to ordinary life, not a fresh set of possessions or a promise that everyone has forgotten what happened.

Local Knowledge and Returning Faces.text:
Glowhaven's recurring people have work, friendships, and obligations outside the player. Established staff handle their actual posts; visitors can become familiar customers, rivals, colleagues, or friends without recruiting anyone. Events can gather familiar faces, but ordinary visits do not summon the entire cast.

Information travels through witnesses, conversation, letters, records, and established magical communication. Shared location is not shared knowledge. A confidence remains private unless disclosed. Rumors can be mistaken; a later correction and an old promise remain part of people's memories.

Fieldwork and Woodland Threats.text:
Glowhaven's nearby fields and woods support ordinary wildlife alongside creatures adapted to dense mana. Damage, tracks, feeding habits, and territory matter before a hunter chooses an approach. A moss-backed boar is a heavy territorial animal whose coat collects soil and moss; its charge is dangerous, but a broken fence does not prove it is hunting people.

Academy fieldwork establishes a route, equipment, supervision, permission, and turnaround before leaving. Observation, protecting crops, relocation, and a justified hunt are different outcomes. Strong instructors remain capable and intervene when students are actually endangered. Their presence does not make poor preparation harmless or guarantee every learning goal succeeds.

Every academy student must complete an authorized expedition beyond the Glowhaven region. School expeditions require the Great Sage or court's actual authorization as well as route, supervision, and local permissions. A hunt is not the only valid educational result; private travel and unrelated casual work do not automatically meet the requirement.

Magical Approaches and Martial Training.text:
Glowhaven distinguishes learned magical disciplines from the approaches through which they are practiced. Logic emphasizes analytical structure and precision, governing Arcane, Metal, Gravity, Enchantment and Space. Passion emphasizes conviction, creative energy and directed release, governing Fire, Lightning, Earth, Wind and Water. Empathy emphasizes relationships with living systems and conceptual balances, governing Healing, Nature, Light, Summoning and Soul. Intuition emphasizes instinctive timing, subconscious recognition and perception beyond deliberate reasoning, governing Divination, Void, Illusion, Ice and Sound.
These approaches describe capabilities rather than moral character or compulsory behavior. A quiet person can work through Passion, a selfish person can practice Healing through Empathy, and an analytical caster can make foolish personal choices. An affinity still makes its school easier to learn; every school remains learnable through study and practice.
Physical training develops Force and Finesse alongside these magical aptitudes. Force includes physical power, resilience, sustained exertion and guarded fighting, while Finesse emphasizes coordination, precision and timing. Spellblades and martial casters combine actual learned magic with powerful, precise or guarded bodily technique. A magical weapon strike depends on its delivery and the actual spell, while a detached or remotely shaped working remains a casting task. Training, equipment, available mana and the intended effect limit what can be achieved; a dramatic description does not supply extra mastery.

The twenty public disciplines now divide evenly across those four magical approaches. Time is a reserved Logic discipline, not a public affinity or starting study. Force and Finesse remain the physical attributes; Stamina is a spendable resource, not a restored Endurance attribute.

Mana, Souls, and Mana Beasts.text:
Mana permeates the environment and can exist inside living beings. Magic is the influence produced by directing mana; internal and ambient describe where the mana is, rather than separate elements. The soul permits intentional circulation of internal mana. Soul-bearing humanoids and mana beasts can cast or naturally employ magic. Dragons, phoenixes, gryffins, and hydras are examples of mana beasts.
Ordinary animals have no souls. They may contain inert internal mana and react to dangerously dense ambient mana, but cannot circulate it or deliberately cast. Possessing mana does not prove that a creature has a soul. A chicken breathing magical fire is an anomaly needing an actual explanation, not ordinary poultry behavior. A pet, an animal familiar, a magical beast, and a summoned construct should not be assigned identical physiology merely because they accompany someone.
The Evertree thickens local mana and makes it easier to sense and work with. It is not the established origin of all mana everywhere, and dense ambient mana is not an inexhaustible immediately usable personal supply.

Mana Capacity, Absorption, and Recovery.text:
A person's mana capacity has an inherited or birth-established component and can grow through repeated use and training. An initially small reserve is not a fixed lifetime ceiling, and an initially large reserve is not a substitute for control. Individual potential cannot be read from school colors, social status, or one observed spell.
The body absorbs ambient mana within a varying ordinary range. Condition and activity matter. Rest, with a clear mind and less competing bodily effort, allows the soul to restore the usable pool more efficiently; sufficient time also permits recovery. Special learned techniques can affect uptake. No universal physical rate, genetic formula, or magic-to-calorie exchange has been established. Ordinary food is nourishment rather than an automatic mana refill; mana-bearing ingredients and regulated medicines are different cases.
A caster can exhaust the usable pool while soul-sustaining internal mana remains. People differ in capacity and control. Improved mana availability does not automatically resolve an underlying medical condition.

Gameplay recovery is resolved on a completed rest or an actual new-day transition, not one refill on every action. Biological ambient absorption does not create passive turn-based Mana regeneration. Explicit mana medicines and dedicated recovery techniques retain their own stated effects.

Mana Exhaustion and the Vital Reserve.text:
Usable casting mana is distinct from the internal remainder that sustains the soul. Ordinary spellcasting cannot consume that protected remainder. Zero usable mana means the caster's spendable pool is exhausted, not that all internal mana has disappeared. Reaching zero alone leaves the caster conscious.
An unaffordable ordinary spell normally fizzles. A deliberately forced last spell at exactly zero can very rarely succeed through an exceptionally difficult authoritative check, extraordinary skill, will, or luck. This is not a dependable free reserve. Repeated forcing causes severe migraines and can make further casting impossible until recovery. A failed or successful desperate cast does not purchase its effect with Health or soul-sustaining mana.
Ordinary self-casting cannot kill someone by emptying the vital remainder. Physical injuries, other causes of unconsciousness, and the actual game's death rules remain separate. Refilling Mana neither revives the dead nor automatically wakes someone unconscious for another reason.

Theoretical Mana Extraction and Soul Sho.text:
Forcibly extracting another person's internal mana is an obscure theoretical possibility with no established witnessed humanoid practitioner, including among known Void mages. Suppression, disruption, sealing, and ordinary spell expenditure are not automatically this technique. An unusual powerful creature with different soul biology might behave differently, but no such enemy or ability is established merely by discussing the possibility.
If actual forced extraction crossed below zero usable mana into the protected remainder, the victim would lose consciousness and suffer mana shock affecting the soul. Negative usable mana is accounting language for a breached threshold, not a physically negative quantity of mana. Complete forced removal of all internal mana would be fatal. If some remains and the victim survives, natural regeneration and appropriate care can support recovery over weeks or months according to severity. Replenishing mana does not instantly cure the shock.
Permanent harm is extremely rare and possible only after abrupt, rapid, powerful shock; gradual depletion does not produce that rare lasting damage under this account. Exact physiology, awakening thresholds, and treatment protocols are not established. Attempting forceful extraction is treated as attempted murder even in a small amount, but an accusation or theoretical discussion is not proof of an attempt. Evidence and actual judiciary decisions still matter.

Body Casting and Catalysts.text:
The body is a normal starting point for learning magic. A mage learns to sense and circulate internal mana, then perform controlled effects through the hands, limbs, or other trained bodily methods. It is difficult initially and becomes more comfortable with practice. Familiar body-cast cantrips are ordinary; expert control can be impressive without making the absence of a staff legendary. Losing a focus does not erase learned spells.
A catalyst is fashioned from mana-bearing materials that help a caster feel, regulate, and direct mana. Crystals, phoenix feathers, and dragon-related materials are examples, without a universal rule about harvesting or ownership. A wand, staff, weapon, accessory, or professional tool can serve; its shape does not decide the school. Suitable materials and affinity compatibility can improve control or impact when used competently, but no universal numeric multiplier or instant mastery follows.
Basic catalysts cost money and are relatively accessible in Glowhaven compared with many foreign markets. A household mage may reasonably do without one. An ordinary memory aid, prop, or unprepared weapon is not automatically a genuine catalyst. Most catalysts assist control rather than supplying a second reservoir.

External Mana Reserves and Tournament Du.text:
Some expensive specialist catalysts contain an external mana reserve. This is not a default feature of every focus and not a third metaphysical kind of mana. Managing it can be awkward, tiring, and inefficient, like controlling another person's limb. It is not automatically merged with the user's internal pool or a way to perform spells beyond their learning. Practical direct injection from such reserves is not solved technology.
During an active tournament duel, competitors may not draw external stored mana from any item or use mana potions. Ordinary control-assisting catalysts remain legal under this rule, and natural ambient uptake is not an illicit item reserve. After an official stop, emergency mana-potion treatment is permitted. A private quarrel, ordinary shopping scene, or unsanctioned spar is not automatically a tournament match.
Officials enforce the announced competition rules using actual observations and evidence. A rule does not make cheating physically impossible or give every referee omniscience. No unannounced prize, bracket, automatic confiscation, or universal detection enchantment follows from this prohibition.

Spell Blueprints and Freeform Casting.text:
A spell is an instructional blueprint guiding mana through a learned operation. Speech, gestures, notation, and components can assist concentration or execution without being universal necessities. Different mages can produce the same recognized effect through personalized blueprints. An instructor can require a method in an exercise without proving every other method invalid.
Studying a school gives access to the familiar introductory effects actually practiced; written spell collections do not exhaust the possibilities of learned magic. A sensible new application of a familiar blueprint is not automatically Freeform casting. Learning, range, control, preparation, and available mana still limit the result.
True Freeform casting constructs the effect without a prepared blueprint. It is rare, highly demanding, and ordinarily slower and less practical because the caster devises the working in real time. Exceptional mastery might overcome some of that burden, but nobody receives it merely by being an Archon, having a rare affinity, or describing a spectacular action. Research and invention can be interesting without supplying instant combat mastery.

Bodily Enchantment and Arcane Wards.text:
Intentional magical increases to bodily strength, speed, resilience, or other physical capabilities are applications of Enchantment. Mana merely circulating through a limb does not grant every enhancement. Advanced bodily enchantment can be extremely powerful, with training, control, and the actual working determining its limits. No arbitrary weak ceiling follows from improving the body instead of throwing a projectile.
A different element can accompany a movement enchantment as a flash, discharge, trail, or attack. That does not require a new affinity: learned competence extends beyond natural affinity. External wind or pressure propelling someone is distinct from strengthening their muscles or altering bodily performance.
Arcane wards can be layered over the body to protect it. They require an actual learned working and do not guarantee invulnerability. Their exact effectiveness against a hypothetical, unobserved soul-extraction method is not an established experimental fact.

Enchantments and Magitech.text:
An enchanted item bears a magical property. Magitech integrates mechanical engineering with magic, enchantments, magical components, or devices. The distinction is the engineered integration, not price, prestige, or whether the object glows. An enchanted necklace is not automatically a machine; an engineered mechanism incorporating a magical driver can be magitech.
Gryffin Tail Academy alone formally specializes in magitech research among Glowhaven's four academies and has the most advanced research infrastructure for that purpose. This is not a ban on other people using, buying, studying, or repairing engineered devices, and ordinary enchanting remains part of the wider city's trade.
Useful direct mana transfusion through engineering remains unachieved. Research and weak prototypes are possible, but they are not standard clinical equipment or reliable instant refills. A visiting student cannot claim a successful medical technology merely by repairing a simple enchanted fitting.

Mana Potions and Magical Medical Care.text:
Mana potions are expensive, regulated medicines that can help restore usable mana. Their existence does not fix one universal dose, price, recovery speed, licensing body, or treatment protocol. An actual preparation must have its own stated strength and appropriate conditions of use.
Excessive use of ordinary consumer-strength potions causes unpleasant and increasingly unhelpful effects such as vomiting, headaches, and diminishing restoration; it cannot cause a fatal overdose. Potentially dangerous high-strength formulations belong only in authorized research and are not presumed to be on sale. Medicine is not an infinite cheap casting loop.
Healing magic primarily treats physical injuries. While channeling it, a skilled healer can feel and assess circulation and may incidentally help it function better. This is not routine extraction, transplantation, or a solved direct mana transfusion. Potions and restored mana do not instantly remove soul shock, aging, or established lasting injuries. Administering a drink to an unconscious patient requires appropriate care rather than assumed normal swallowing.

Authorized Student Expeditions.text:
Every student at all four academies must complete at least one expedition outside the entire Glowhaven region. The requirement means a distant regional assignment, not a walk beyond Glowhaven City's walls. The city's farms, nearby woods, Greywatch Keep, coastal settlements, islands and Wraith Island remain local; Wraith Island Prison is also ineligible. The current distant destination maps are Drakenspire Mountains and Asterveil Sky Archipelago.
The Great Sage or court authorizes the actual mission: purpose, destination, route/site, scope, supervision, participants and return/debrief arrangements. Travel can use the Portal Room at Evertree Base when passage is arranged. Authorization does not require the Great Sage to accompany everyone or confer command over a foreign community. Transit access is distinct from permission to enter a protected habitat, workshop or relic site.
All academies share the requirement while approaching fieldwork through their actual mandates. Protection, logistics, negotiation, survey, craft investigation, preservation and permitted recovery can be valid tasks. Actual authorized travel beyond Glowhaven, completed fieldwork and a truthful received report establish completion. Local practice, private tourism, merely crossing a portal, accepting another job or witnessing another student's work is not credit. Safety can require withdrawal or a revised assignment. A routine level-twenty field test is a separate academy exercise, not this expedition requirement. Its postponement never completes or cancels an authorized expedition. Visiting adults and people outside the academies may join an approved assignment voluntarily; their presence does not make them students.

Exploration, Relics, and Stewardship.text:
Dragon Hoard Academy's exploration and relic work concerns what a team can find, understand, handle, and responsibly bring back from an unfamiliar place. An unexcavated site, damaged inscription, unstable object, disputed find, or difficult return journey can matter without a new world-threatening artifact.
Survey and documentation can be valuable outcomes. Recovery requires the actual mission's authority and applicable permission; finding an object does not establish ownership, and taking it is not automatically the best solution. Preservation, stabilizing a site, identifying a hazard, leaving an object in place, or arranging lawful custody may be the sound result. Existing owners, communities, courts, and offices retain their claims and responsibilities. No universal salvage code or new relic bureaucracy is presumed.
The school's inherited strictness can appear through exact preparation and instructors' different judgments about acceptable risk. It does not make every student acquisitive, disciplined, curious, or brave. Tōru Shizunami's personality and the existing cast remain their own.

Evertree Portals and Distant Regions.text:
The Portal Room at Evertree Base links Glowhaven with distant regions of the same world. These passages connect distant physical places in the same world. The current routes lead to Drakenspire Mountains and Asterveil Sky Archipelago. Wraith Island Prison is a separate secured map of Glowhaven's offshore prison, not a distant expedition destination or a portal stop.
The room opens from Rear Palace Walk through a controlled transit entrance. Travelers need actual permission and an available route; an authorized expedition can establish these arrangements. Transit permission grants access to the route and its arrival area, not every palace room, Evertree root or foreign restricted site. An approved visitor, trader, escort, researcher or noncasting traveler can use an operating portal; passengers need not cast the gate themselves.
Each route has an arrival and return point: Drakenspire's Portal Room and Cloudbloom Landing's Portal Room connect to Glowhaven's Portal Room. Choose and actually enter the named open portal; discussing travel or standing nearby does not move the party. Permits, cargo limits, escorts or a fare must be established in the actual scene rather than invented as a universal schedule or price. Other lands exist beyond these established routes. Passage to one requires a genuine route and destination.
Issued reusable transit keys select the ordinary routes in the Portal Room. An authorized passenger need not cast or keep paying mana to hold the gate open. A key records its actual passage and is retained after use; return traffic uses the destination's existing arrival arch. Each ordinary destination has a dedicated enclosed Portal Room: basalt and iron in Drakenspire, living whitewood and translucent glass at Cloudbloom Landing. Crossing lands inside that room, not at an outdoor gate or a random island. Leaving the room and returning home are separate choices. The Silken Descent is the anomalous exception, whose existing threshold return arch remains immediately usable.

Evertree Base - Portal Room is the sole Glowhaven portal hub. Every established external return arch has that exact fixed endpoint. Entering a return arch completes the crossing there; it does not ask the traveler to select a neighborhood, academy or generic city arrival. Choosing to leave the hub afterward is a separate action.

Drakenspire Mountains.text:
Drakenspire is an independent dragonkin-majority nation and the name of its snowy mountain capital. The city occupies two nearby elevations: a bustling inhabited shelf below, and Crescent Crown Fortress on a higher northeastern shelf. An enormous sacred dragon skeleton curves around the fortress in a crescent, joining stone walls and ancient bones into the country's defining landmark. The remains commemorate the dragon that protected the endangered founders; they do not power the city's heat or magic.

Practical alpine stone buildings, steep cobbled lanes, heavy shutters and wool-bright interiors characterize the lower city. The fortress government is sturdy rather than extravagant, while a few wealthy commercial buildings advertise private prosperity. Markets, homes, workshops, inns, a modest schoolhouse, festival streets, a small fight pit and one onsen support ordinary life. Dragon and ancestor worship shapes public customs without making every resident equally devout or every dragonkin a warrior.

A Jarl elected through the clan chiefs governs within a decentralized clan-and-chief order. Clans retain substantial influence, alongside merchants and military leaders. Drakenspire and Glowhaven are friendly sovereign partners: this country supplies excellent metallurgy and valuable magical raw materials, while Glowhaven provides enchanted goods, specialist education and other trade. The enclosed Drakenspire - Portal Room receives authorized travelers and connects to Evertree Base - Portal Room under the existing key rules.

Beyond the inhabited shelves lie lower pastures, sparse pine hollows, mines, abandoned workings, neighboring peaks and dangerous snowbound country. Some routes suit prepared fieldwork; others reach wyvern perches, giant territory or rarely visited basins. Sacred dragons discourage many threats from approaching the capital without constantly fighting on its streets. A vast gray, lightning-breathing guardian sometimes appears far overhead. His lair, the number of dragons and the full history of their generations remain unknown to the people.

Asterveil Sky Archipelago.text:
Asterveil is a broad archipelago of floating islands in the same physical world as Glowhaven. Four mapped regions surround a small fae settlement: Cloudbloom Reaches in the northwest, Rimeglass Heights in the northeast, Mirrorwater Marches in the southwest and Amethyst Crown in the southeast. The realm is predominantly wilderness, with scattered field shelters rather than four towns. Cloudbloom Landing receives the authorized Evertree portal route; Asterveil Canopy is the settlement near it.

Fae live alongside a smaller number of other residents. Flower terraces, craft, fragrance cultivation, weather study and crossing work support daily life, while expeditions investigate plants, creatures, materials and the remains of earlier survey work. Residents are people with varied goals, not universal guides, miniature mascots or custodians of every secret. Some individuals can change size; their actual record determines their forms.

This is a midgame expedition realm. Normal regional bands progress through 8–20, 15–30, 25–40 and 35–50. Safe hubs have lower local bands. The Inverted Crown is an exceptional level-48–55 field site, not an endgame zone. A young visiting player is not barred by an invisible level wall, and a powerful visiting NPC keeps their actual level. Risk is communicated through local evidence and available preparation.

Known Routes and Distant Lands.text:
Glowhaven encompasses the city, nearby settlements, farms, woods, rivers, islands and familiar coast. Drakenspire Mountains and Asterveil Sky Archipelago are distant regions reached through the Evertree's established portal routes. Wraith Island Prison occupies the secured campus on Glowhaven's offshore prison island.
These routes are the destinations currently served from Evertree Base. The wider world contains other lands and peoples; a familiar route is not a boundary to existence. Travelers seek actual directions, a chart, a guide or an established passage when planning a journey. A court order for an expedition does not confer ownership of foreign property or authority over another community.

The Great Sage and the Archons.text:
The Great Sage governs Glowhaven and directs the city's public response to serious threats. The Archons represent their academies on the Conclave and exercise their own expertise and judgment; a Conclave seat is not exemption from the city's lawful government. Headmasters run the academic systems beneath them.
An envoy carries only the authority actually delegated. A genuine credential identifies its bearer and office; the accompanying order establishes the task. Once accepted, officials carry out that task within its scope rather than beginning the same identification dispute again at every sentence. Professional disagreement can change a practical plan without becoming a contest over whether the city has a ruler.

Academy Enrollment and Daily Life.text:
An academy First Day begins with an already-enrolled adult first-year, not a second application. The new academic year starts across the whole school. Newcomers collect timetables at the registrar's desk, gather with the other first-years for the headmaster's welcome, then attend the first Magic Theory lesson. Returning students follow their own year schedules.

Morning lessons are required. Each academy rotates its three core subjects on issued timetables, while afternoons normally leave time for lunch, clubs, supervised practice, study, friends and outside life. Examinations or announced practicals can need extra time. Instructors teach their actual subjects in appropriate rooms; affinity is not a class assignment.

Headmasters normally work in Faculty Offices, leaving for scheduled welcomes or other real duties. New instructors are told their subject, classroom and next-morning first-bell appointment; their first day allows questions, meeting the department and preparing an achievable lesson. Existing professors keep their posts. Other adults can visit, trade or work without enrolling.

Court Oracle.text: Mihoshi Kagamihara serves Ilyra Stillglass as the Great Sage's court oracle. Her divination supports warnings, investigations and difficult decisions. She distinguishes a seen fragment from an inference and a claim from a verified report. A vision does not make every future inevitable. She receives visitors at the court observatory.

Portal Keys and Passage.text: Ordinary travelers request a Drakenspire or Asterveil transit key at the court's public transit counter, or through an official arranging their mission. The issued key records a genuine passage on its named operating route and is retained after use. Its holder opens that route in Evertree Base's Portal Room; approved companions can travel with them without each casting the gate. A simple request for ordinary passage does not require a personal audience with the Great Sage. A lost key can be replaced through an actual new handover. Transit does not open private chambers, erase a criminal warrant or decide a foreign property claim. After the first real Evertree crossing, travelers receive a reusable Glowhaven Portal Key identifying the return to Evertree Base - Portal Room. Use it only at an existing destination return arch; it is not a recall spell from arbitrary terrain. The fixed return arches remain usable without it. Returning requires no additional city landing choice and does not move a traveler into other palace rooms. The court controls outbound access. A traveler must present a legitimate reason and actually receive the court-issued route key. Enrolled academy students have the easiest ordinary route to eligibility; authorized merchants, court staff on duty and nobles with credible connections or sponsorship can also qualify. Status alone is not an automatic key grant. The court or an explicitly delegated court official decides and records the actual permission. A helpful acquaintance, porter or apprentice cannot create authorization merely by offering a key. Existing valid authorization is not reopened at every crossing.  The Glowhaven return key is issued under the already approved passage, and fixed return arches remain available for the journey home.

Academy Years and Academic Standing.text: Each of Glowhaven's four academies offers a four-year program. All current academy students are adults aged at least eighteen. Academic year records progress through the curriculum, not age, combat level or a mandatory class cohort. Later enrollment, transfers and different rates of progress are possible, but do not invent such a history merely to explain someone's year. The selected cast is a sample of each academy, not every enrolled student; a year need not have a named representative. Friends, rivals and club members can be in different years. Use each student's actual Academic standing rather than making every student a new entrant or graduating all party members together.

The Silken Brood.text: The arachne matron and the creatures defending the inner workings of the Silken Chasm. Their motives and reactions differ; a passage can sometimes be bypassed without exterminating every creature.

Glowhaven.text:
Glowhaven is the civic community and autonomous polity centered on the Evertree: the city, surrounding villages, farms, waterways and coast. Its mostly human population includes long-settled nonhuman residents and foreign newcomers. The Great Sage governs through the court, the larger council, public offices and ordinary working institutions. The four academies are prominent parts of public life, not the whole population. Residents include growers, fishers, shopkeepers, craftspeople, tenants, porters, householders, students and people who simply want a dependable livelihood.
A civic affiliation identifies belonging and everyday obligations; it does not mean employment by the state, personal loyalty to the Great Sage or membership in every local guild. A person can be a Glowhaven resident while their primary roster faction is an academy, guard service, household or trade organization. People without a more specific institutional affiliation normally use Glowhaven. Visitors, unaffiliated wanderers and wild creatures need not be assigned here just because they are currently present.
Enchanted goods, agricultural produce, fisheries, shipping, repairs, hospitality and research sustain the region. Permits, housing, wages, public safety, tournaments and access to the dense local mana create real negotiations. Membership supplies no free money, unrestricted research access, court title or portal key. Court-approved passage requires an actual reason and issue.

Drakenspire.text:
Drakenspire is an independent dragonkin-majority nation whose mountain capital bears the same name. Its people live beneath a high northeastern fortress and the sacred crescent of an ancient protector dragon's skeleton. A Jarl elected through the clan chiefs governs with substantial local clan autonomy; merchants, craft interests and military leaders also influence public decisions. Ordinary residents include workers, families, traders, scholars and people of other species, not a uniform warrior caste.

Dragon and ancestor worship, winter hospitality, practical craft and collective memories of the founding give the country a recognizable culture. Households vary in belief, wealth and conduct. The local economy combines advanced metallurgy, magical raw materials, livestock, trade and many ordinary services. Drakenspire is a friendly sovereign partner of Glowhaven, with authorized portal travel and strong links between its materials and Glowhaven's enchanted-goods industry. A visitor's connections abroad do not make them an officer of the hold.

Asterveil.text: Asterveil is the civic community of the inhabited sky archipelago, centered on the small Asterveil Canopy settlement. Fae households and residents of other peoples cultivate gardens, make fragrances and tools, carry freight and support fieldwork. A household assembly appoints rotating stewards for practical duties; the realm is independent and cooperates with Glowhaven through agreed travel and exchange. Citizenship does not make all wild creatures allies or make every resident a guide. Use this affiliation for local residents without a narrower organization; visiting academy members keep their actual affiliation.

The Great Sage's Court.text:
The Great Sage's Court is the working household and administrative service supporting Ilyra Stillglass and Glowhaven's government. It includes attendants, public clerks, court advisers, messengers, transit staff, research liaisons and people entrusted with defined duties. It is distinct from the larger elected governing council and from the Conclave of Archons. Service at court grants the authority of the actual office, not the Great Sage's personal powers.
The court processes appointments, petitions, official communication, expedition authorization and controlled portal access. An enrolled student's legitimate study, approved trade, court duty or credible noble sponsorship can support a passage request. A real official must approve and issue the key; a porter, visiting student or friendly acquaintance cannot do so. Ordinary approved passage does not require a personal audience with Ilyra Stillglass. Once established, valid permission is preserved within scope.
Future court staff can have sharply different competence, loyalties and manner. An attendant may assist the Great Sage's failing sight without knowing every political plan. A transit clerk may authorize routine passage without gaining access to the Evertree's most sensitive work.

Wraith Island Prison Administration.text:
The prison administration serves the court through custody officers, clerks, medical staff, work supervisors, storekeepers and transport workers. A person’s duties determine their authority. Guards do not decide guilt by themselves, a healer can insist on treatment without ordering a legal discharge, and an intake clerk does not command the whole island. Prisoners, contractors and visitors retain their different roles.

Officers work shifts, facilities need maintenance and supply runs can be delayed by sea conditions. The institution is staffed by people with their own loyalties and limits, rather than an all-knowing presence.

Glowhaven Trade Guild.text:
Glowhaven Trade Guild is a voluntary association of merchants, stallholders, brokers and carriers. It offers introductions, shared market information, contract advice and mediation for members. It works with harbor, market and court offices but is not the government, a universal shop chain or an authority over every trader. A merchant can operate independently.
Future members may include traveling sellers, import agents, warehouse partners, apprentices and petty rivals. Membership and reputation depend on the actual person and history, not wealth alone. Work can involve delivery, appraisal, commission disputes and stock problems. Terms, fees and payments must be established rather than invented as automatic dues. The guild can support a court application for legitimate trade passage; it cannot mint its own official portal keys.

Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.text:
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild is a voluntary professional network for craft workers, repairers and enchantment specialists. Smiths, joiners, leatherworkers, jewellers, alchemists and practical enchanters can exchange referrals, workspace knowledge and advice while retaining independent shops and methods. The guild does not own every workshop or make all enchanted goods magitech.
Its practical influence comes from workmanship, repeat customers and professional trust. Future members can seek apprentices, materials, a fair commission or recognition for a method. A referral is not a free item, a guaranteed result or proof of mastery. Clients own entrusted goods unless actual terms say otherwise. Prices and repair scope are agreed before work, and failed or completed commissions remain consequences rather than resetting on each visit.

House Goldbarrow.text:
House Goldbarrow is the noble household associated with House Goldbarrow Estate in Glowhaven. Its household members, employees and actual agents have different standing and duties. Hanae Goldbarrow manages routine purchases and receives tradespeople at the estate. The house participates in the city's property, patronage and commercial life without representing every noble family.
Future relatives, retainers, advisers and hired specialists belong here only when the relationship is established. A visitor, tenant, customer or worker on one commission is not automatically a household member. Noble connections can support a court request but are not a portal key or universal immunity. Household wealth does not make every relative a combat expert or every servant a secret spy.

Creatures and Constructed Beings.text: Ordinary wildlife, mana beasts, sapient peoples, animated constructs and restless dead are different kinds of beings. Ordinary animals do not deliberately cast magic; a mana beast's actual trained or innate abilities govern what it can do. Fae, dragonkin and beastfolk have individual occupations, beliefs and relationships rather than a compulsory animal temperament. A construct's behavior depends on its real design, control and awareness. A supernatural remnant has a particular origin and limits, not universal knowledge. Encounters belong to suitable habitats and actual situations. Tracks, workings, behavior and local testimony can provide fair warning; observation, avoidance, handling and negotiation can matter alongside fighting. A defeated or bypassed territorial creature does not return as an identical replacement merely because its species still exists.

Field Tests and the Anomalous Passage.text: A routine academy field test becomes due for enrolled students around level twenty; accepted adult volunteers can also participate. Ordinary instructions and court passage permission encourage a legitimate visit to the Evertree Portal Room. A briefing neither arms nor predicts an anomaly. The first actual normal Drakenspire or Asterveil crossing by a traveling player party containing a level-twenty-or-higher player is interrupted once into the Silken Descent, whether or not a field-test quest was accepted. It does not recur on later crossings. Staff do not know this cause or destination in advance. The party arrives together inside a ruined portal room with possessions intact, a silver-threaded key manifests, and the home arch is usable immediately. The separate investigation lead becomes available on discovery; descent is optional. After return, any outstanding field-test sitting is cancelled and postponed without a passed-test award or invented new date. The mandatory authorized expedition remains a different assignment with its own permission, actual distant fieldwork and received report. The Silken investigation and its boss outcome grant no automatic expedition credit.

Phoenix Wing Academy — Core Subjects.text: Phoenix Wing Academy has three named core teaching appointments: Magic Theory — Haruki Saitō; Magical Combat — Ritsu Kurogane; Potions & Alchemy — Ranka Kagari. Common principles feed into supervised duels and laboratory practice. Students can connect an explanation to a controlled fight or test a formula with actual ingredients. Magic Theory is common to all four academies; the other two core subjects differ. These are broad subjects, not affinity-only tracks. A professor's innate affinity, practiced specialization and teaching appointment are separate facts.
