Every school of magic remains learnable, and examples or demonstrations need not use a student's own affinity. Subjects provide instructional situations using existing skills and learning rules; attending a lesson does not automatically award a skill, spell or mastery. Clubs, supervised practice, independent study and broader academic work can also occur without creating additional named core professors. The three subjects are required parts of the morning curriculum, rotated on the issued year timetable; afternoons are normally free. They are not three optional enrollment tracks.

Engineering treats integrated magical/mechanical systems; arts gives the research-heavy campus a visibly different kind of classroom. Dragonkin Appearance and Anatomy.text:
Dragonkin are mostly humanoid people of roughly human height, with human faces, dragonlike horns, scales along the sides of their faces and vertical slit pupils. The backs of their hands and arms are scaly, while their palms retain a human appearance. They have thick dragon tails. Individual colors and the amount of visible scaling vary. Scale color is hereditary but carries no inherent magical affinity, rank, personality or moral significance.

Dragonkin can live up to about two hundred years. Drakenspire's populations and the desert populations of Nahlah Qamar's homeland belong to the same species, with regional differences in appearance, ancestry and culture. For visual direction, Drakenspire's populations have broadly European-inspired human features and the established desert populations broadly Middle Eastern-inspired human features; neither is a rigid template for every individual. Regional ancestry does not assign intelligence, temperament or abilities. Dragonkin are people, not lesser dragons or wyverns. Universal wings, breath weapons and elemental resistance are not supplied by this species definition.

Drakenspire Clan Assembly.text: The gathering of clan chiefs through which the Jarl is chosen and major shared obligations are debated. It provides a forum for cross-clan disputes, commitments and national decisions within a decentralized order. Merchants, military leaders and witnesses may influence deliberations without all becoming chiefs or automatic electors. The assembly works alongside the Jarl rather than serving as a second royal dynasty.

Drakenspire Hold Guard.text: The local force responsible for gates, public order, road patrols and immediate defense under Drakenspire's government. It works from practical barracks and watchposts, enforcing the ban on street dueling and responding to actual danger. Its personnel are residents with jobs and private lives, not an extension of Glowhaven's elite strikeforce.

Keepers of the Crescent.text: Custodians of Drakenspire's dragon-and-ancestor observances, the sacred ancestral skeleton, sanctuary records and associated memorial sites. They organize care, remembrance and public ceremonies while working with stoneworkers and households. Their authority concerns religious custody and practice; they do not command living dragons or guarantee divine favors.

Clan Iwatsugu.text: One of the prominent clans with a capital clanhold. Historic involvement in stonework, quarrying and early settlement works gives it influence in public construction and repair. Its households and associates follow varied occupations; the clan is a network of kinship, obligations and history rather than a compulsory professional caste.

Clan Yukinose.text: A prominent clan connected with provisions, rural households, husbandry and the maintenance of routes linking settlements to the capital. Its capital house receives travelers, messages and practical requests. These associations describe influence and history, not ownership of every pasture or monopoly over all food.

Clan Arashimine.text: A prominent clan with historic ties to arms-making and military service. Its capital house supports contracts, family obligations and questions of readiness. Its influence does not make every member a soldier or give relatives personal command over the hold guard.

Drakenspire — Founding and the Ancestral.text:
The founders reached the mountain exhausted and close to death. An ancient dragon protected them, giving the small community the chance to survive and establish its first shelters. The settlement later developed mining and the trades that made continued life on the mountain possible. Its growth was gradual: houses, routes, stores and defenses followed the need to remain through winter.

The protector's enormous skeleton now lies in a crescent around the higher northeastern fortress shelf. Drakenspire treats these remains as sacred history, an enduring reminder that the first inhabitants survived through protection they could not have secured alone. Keepers care for the bones and their setting; worshippers approach on maintained paths. The skeleton is not a source of building material, a public dungeon or the magical engine of the city. Its importance is religious, historical and visual. The ancient dragon's personal name and the precise circumstances of its death are not established by the surviving public account.

Drakenspire — Upper Fortress and Lower C.text:
The capital is divided between two nearby elevations on a snowy mountain. Crescent Crown Fortress occupies the higher northeastern shelf, with defensive walls, courts, government halls and religious precincts. Below it, most people live and work on a broader shelf of steep lanes, stone houses, markets and workshops. The ancestral skeleton curves around the upper stronghold; together they form one dominant skyline landmark.

Construction favors thick stone, pitched roofs, covered entrances, shutters, drains and practical routes for freight. The governing buildings are substantial and restrained rather than uniformly palatial. Coppercrest Exchange and a few other wealthy businesses can be more conspicuously ornate. Lower-city streets make room for dragon festivals and ordinary traffic. The region includes surrounding slopes and neighboring mountains, so the capital is dense without filling the whole map with urban buildings.

Drakenspire — The Jarl and the Clans.text:
Drakenspire is a decentralized elective monarchy rooted in clans and chiefs. The chiefs choose the Jarl; inheriting a clan household does not inherit national rule. The current Jarl is Daizen Iwatsugu, an elderly dragonkin and former adventurer. Against his family’s wishes he spent his younger life adventuring. He returned as an older man, took up his deceased father’s responsibilities as Iwatsugu chief and eventually accepted election as Jarl in his honor.

Clan Iwatsugu, Clan Yukinose and Clan Arashimine are the three prominent capital clans. They are kinship and obligation networks with historical economic associations, not compulsory professional castes. Tsubaki Iwatsugu runs much Iwatsugu household administration. Masatsugu Yukinose leads Yukinose; Tomoe Arashimine leads Arashimine. Their rivalry is bitter and the peace fragile, but local life continues. Merchants, military leaders, witnesses and smaller households influence choices without automatically becoming electoral chiefs. Norse and Gaelic traditions inspire institutional texture; humanoid personal names retain Japanese-inspired given-name-first order.

Drakenspire — Dragon and Ancestor Worshi.text:
Dragons are sacred beings in Drakenspire, and the ancient protector's refuge is central to the nation's memory. Ancestor remembrance honors the people who maintained homes, routes, craft and kin through a difficult environment. The two traditions share public festivals, memorial practice and a sense of inherited obligation, without making every family equally devout.

The Keepers of the Crescent maintain the sanctuary, sacred paths and memorial records. Offerings can express gratitude or hope, but do not purchase a dragon's obedience or guarantee supernatural intervention. Visitors may ask questions, observe or behave respectfully without being forced to profess faith. Ordinary offenses against people and property remain distinct from theological disagreement. A pious citizen can be funny, vain, generous or impatient; belief does not replace personality.

Drakenspire — The Gray Guardian.text:
Rovakthuun is the individual behind the Gray Guardian sightings: an immense gray dragon with four legs, two separate wings, electric-blue eyes and lightning breath. He is a wise, patient spellcaster, feeds on wildlife, monsters and occasional offerings, and speaks slowly with archaic concrete language when he chooses to speak. He is not a humanoid with wings.

Most people know a distant silhouette and uncertain reports, not his personal acquaintance, movements, name or home. His lair remains unknown and is not a discoverable map location. His high flights can warn of danger without predicting its exact form or promising immediate intervention. Generations of sacred dragons are associated with the ranges; their full numbers and relations remain unknown.

A sincere long watch can still find only weather. A prayer, offering, demand, purchased rumor or map click does not summon him. Rare close contact depends on his own interest and the actual encounter, not the player insisting that he appears. No required ordinary commission depends on receiving his help. Preserve his unique record, autonomy and actual injuries or agreements across meetings.

Drakenspire — Dragons, Wyverns and the C.text:
Sacred dragons and wyverns are different creatures. The local guardian has four legs and two wings; wyverns are much smaller two-legged winged predators whose shrieks, nests and territorial behavior make some routes troublesome. Residents regard wyverns as pests and usually avoid their nesting ground rather than routinely culling it. Dragons look down on and dislike wyverns, but this does not promise immediate intervention whenever a traveler is threatened.

The mountains hold many more dangerous creatures than the city streets. The presence of dragons helps keep serious threats from approaching the capital, even though people seldom witness direct intervention. This is a strong ecological deterrent, not an impenetrable magical barrier. Local guards, route workers and sensible preparation still matter. Mountain wildlife belongs in actual terrain and circumstances, not in an indoor portal reception merely because a traveler has arrived.

Drakenspire — Metalwork and Spellblade C.text:
Drakenspire is known for advanced metallurgy and the quality of its weapons, tools and protective equipment. Working mines supply material, foundries prepare stock and specialist shops turn it into finished commissions. Spellblades seek its workshops for weapons balanced and constructed to support their particular casting and fighting methods. Ordinary workmanship, enchantment and magitech are related markets, not interchangeable labels.

A commission begins with use, materials, fit and cost. A weapon can be excellent without being ornate, while an elaborate piece may suit a wealthy customer's taste without exceeding every practical alternative. Skilled construction supports abilities the wielder actually possesses; equipment does not automatically teach magic or create an external mana reserve. Repair, proofing, sourcing a difficult material and resolving a faulty specification can all become worthwhile adventures without requiring a legendary artifact.

Drakenspire — Crystals, Amber and Creatu.text:
The mountains yield mana-bearing crystals and amber valuable to enchanting, magitech construction, alchemy and other craft. Local creatures and mana beasts also provide materials difficult to obtain elsewhere. Provenance, condition, handling and usable yield determine what a specimen is worth; a strange-looking object is not necessarily a rare reagent.

Working sites have owners, crews and access conditions, while wilderness collection needs an actual purpose and a safe route. Assessment and preparation connect collectors with artisans instead of making every find an instantly usable magical item. Trade with Glowhaven links raw resources and metalwork to a large enchanted-goods industry. The existing item and currency rules still govern transactions and effects; descriptive richness does not create a second resource system or a guaranteed restoration value for raw mana-bearing matter.

Drakenspire — Gifts Left by Dragons.text:
Living dragons occasionally leave unfertilized eggs for the people. These rare gifts contain highly sought-after mana-bearing material. They are not viable eggs waiting to hatch, ordinary food with guaranteed restorative effects or a repeatable supply on a predictable schedule. People also prize naturally shed dragon scales, and may pray for the chance to receive one.

Discovering a possible gift calls for care: establish what it is, where it came from, its condition and who has a legitimate claim or responsibility. A shrine offering site does not become a free treasure dispenser. Sacred status and practical use can produce sincere debate, particularly when a material might support valuable craft. None of this authorizes harvesting the ancestral skeleton or hunting a sacred dragon for parts.

Drakenspire — Water, Warmth and Food.text:
Deep mountain aquifers supply water through maintained works and protected distribution. Geothermal sources provide useful warmth where accessible, including the single public bathhouse, Stonewake Onsen, on a lower ledge. The city survives through engineering, fuel, shelter, labor and trade; the ancient bones do not heat it.

Goats and sheep are important to nearby husbandry, supplying meat, dairy and wool. Pastures and winter shelters occupy suitable lower slopes rather than impossible fields across every summit. Stored feed, preserved provisions and portal or overland imports remain necessary. Meat dishes, stews, bread and cheese are common comforts, while imported vegetables and other ingredients vary with supply. Household routines, food stores and water maintenance give the country a believable daily life beyond its military and religious identity.

Drakenspire — Education and Learned Work.text:
Cinderstone Schoolhouse is a modest medium-sized institution providing ordinary education in reading, arithmetic, local history and practical foundations. Community and adult lessons can use its rooms at suitable times. Drakenspire does not possess a large magical academy matching Glowhaven's four schools. People seeking serious magical education commonly go to Glowhaven and may return with new skills, relationships and ambitions.

Local expertise is nevertheless substantial. Smiths, assayers, hunters, healers, surveyors and other practitioners learn through work, instruction and individual study. A lack of a grand institute does not make the population ignorant or unable to use magic. Stonefang provides practical training; assay houses perform professional assessment; the ruined Stormscar station was a weather and signal facility. None becomes a fifth academy merely because scholars visit it.

Drakenspire — Law, Guards and Public Fig.text:
The hold guard handles gates, public order, road reports and the immediate defense of inhabited places. It is a local force under Drakenspire's government, distinct from Glowhaven's guard and elite strikeforce. Public disputes can be taken to the Hold's Judgment House, with larger political questions reaching the appropriate chiefs or the Jarl.

Dueling in the streets is forbidden. The Cinder Pit provides a compact venue for properly arranged public bouts, while Stonefang supports supervised training. Rules, consent and stopping conditions belong to the actual session; healing magic does not make assault harmless. Foreign rank and a court-issued portal key do not confer police powers here. Arrest, evidence custody and sentencing follow actual events and local decisions, rather than applying Glowhaven's island-prison destination automatically.

Drakenspire — Festivals and Ordinary Com.text:
The lower city makes room for frequent dragon-related festivals and ancestor observances. Founders' Processional Way provides broad passage for groups, musicians and temporary stalls, while the sanctuary and households maintain their own customs. Preparation involves labor, food, cleaning, costumes, repair and arguments over space as much as solemn ritual.

Daily life is warmer and more varied than the fortress silhouette suggests. Taverns serve workers and travelers; performances include comedy; shops pursue fashion as well as practicality. Thick wool, fur and layered clothing suit the climate without making everyone look identical. Not every day is a festival, every meal a quest hook or every resident an embodiment of national tradition.

Drakenspire — The Glowhaven Partnership.text:
Drakenspire and Glowhaven are friendly allies who benefit from sustained trade, study and travel. Mountain materials and specialist metalwork complement Glowhaven's enchanted-item industry and magical education. Their relationship does not erase differences in government, religion or law. A Drakenspire resident studying abroad remains connected to a separate homeland rather than becoming a provincial Glowhaven subject.

The permanent crossing arrives inside Drakenspire - Portal Room, an enclosed basalt transit hall, and returns to Evertree Base - Portal Room. Travelers need the established court-issued authorization and route keys; their purpose may involve study, trade, official service or another legitimate reason. A valid crossing does not grant access to private workshops, sacred remains, restricted workings or government interiors. Overland local journeys remain possible without turning every gate into a magical portal.

Drakenspire — Mountain Expeditions and R.text:
The highlands support excursions of different lengths and difficulty. Rimecrest Trail and nearby hollows offer prepared travelers route surveys, ecological observation and manageable fieldwork. Working mines and craft sites involve permissions and industrial hazards. Farther peaks, ravines, caves and creature territories demand more capable parties, appropriate equipment and an honest willingness to retreat.

Avalanches, exposure, unstable ice, loose rock and territorial beasts are real possibilities, not mandatory events on every journey. Tracks, weather reports, damaged structures and local advice give people grounds for decisions before a confrontation. Monster hunting, material collection, relic research and trade are distinct purposes. An authorized academy expedition requires its actual assigned work and debrief; a portal arrival or unrelated fight does not fulfill it. The separate postponed regional field-test incident remains its own existing questline.

Drakenspire — Giants and the Rare Yeti.text:
Mountain giants occupy remote parts of the ranges, leaving signs that can be studied before anyone approaches. Their size makes even ordinary movement dangerous to smaller people, but a particular giant's intelligence, speech and intentions must be established individually. A camp is a place of occupation, not inherently a boss arena full of ownerless treasure.

Yeti are real: rare, isolated giants adapted to remote snowbound country. Most local people know only disputed accounts, unusual tracks or stories from other travelers. Their actual existence is a setting fact, while their location and behavior are not common knowledge. The White Silence is possible habitat, not a guaranteed lair or an encounter that must occur when the player reaches a map marker. Observation, uncertainty and respectful withdrawal can matter as much as combat.

Drakenspire — Old Workings and Founding.text:
Abandoned shafts, haul systems and settlements record changes in mineral yields, routes and the cost of living on difficult ground. Old Hearthfall dwindled as work moved; the Chainworks became impractical to maintain. Such places need no universal massacre or curse to be worth exploring. They can hold engineering history, family belongings, hazards and unresolved property claims.

Founding shelters and old shrines carry different significance from an industrial salvage site. Research should preserve context, distinguish interpretation from certainty and respect actual custodians. A relic can be historically valuable without being a weapon. Most important public places are mapped, while a few obscure sites require discovery. The guardian dragon's home is not one of those discoverable map locations: no confirmed lair is established.

Asterveil Geography and Buoyancy.text:
The four regions form a contiguous two-by-two map. Cloudbloom is northwest, Rimeglass northeast, Mirrorwater southwest and Amethyst southeast. Each holds several large and medium islands, with small fragments between them. The settlement occupies a protected satellite near Cloudbloom’s southeastern side; the wilderness landmass around it is much larger than the inhabited footprint.

Mana-bearing rootstone supports the islands’ buoyancy. Its large formations are stable on ordinary travel timescales; their existence does not make every loose rock float, power a free personal flight spell or provide an inexhaustible generator. Short-term measurements concern wind, load, erosion and local vibration, not an inevitable collapse of all Asterveil. The origin of the oldest suspended foundations remains only partially understood.

The northeastern plateaus rise into colder air; southwestern basins trap water and mist; southeastern mineral ridges carry wind and violet heath. Waterfalls leave real island edges. Lakes and streams are not secretly continuous across sky gaps. No additional realm or unmapped continent is created beneath a fall.

Asterveil Crossings and Field Safety.text:
Only the Cloudbloom Landing Portal Room connects to Glowhaven. Court-issued Asterveil keys retain their actual permissions; local crossing tickets do not replace them. The existing fixed return works without a second key or new court approval. Local movement uses paths on continuous land, short maintained spans where actually present, working boats on water and attended carrier crossings over wider sky gaps.

The Asterveil Crossing Cooperative maintains routes from Cloudbloom toward Tetherroot Chain and Rimeglass Refuge. Tetherroot connects south to Reedglass Anchorage; both the anchorage and refuge have routes toward Heatherwatch Shelf. A light sail carrier uses a real hull, harness, trained crew and controlled lift; it is not an invented free teleport or an unlimited autonomous flying item. Nonflying travelers can buy a seat or join an agreed expedition charter. Short local seats are commonly 12–20 marks, longer regional seats 25–40; cargo, weather and rescue work require a clear actual quote. These are route anchors, not charges applied without a transaction.

A booking includes its actual destination, landing, load and return arrangement. Flights and boats can be unavailable for a real reason without every journey becoming a permit quest. Individual flight still needs a real bodily or learned ability, range, load capacity and safe landing. Small fae wings are not proof of the endurance to carry an adult companion. Strong wind, cold, water and falls are real hazards. Strenuous travel consumes stamina, while preparation, shelter and rescue can make the difference between a difficult crossing and a disaster.

Asterveil Civic Life.text:
Asterveil Canopy is a small independent community linked to Glowhaven by a practical treaty of transit and exchange. Its household assembly appoints rotating stewards for water, crossings and habitat agreements. Open hearings resolve specific disputes; the stewards do not administer every wild nest or command foreign academies. Foreign visitors obey local rules while academy members keep their existing affiliation.

The settlement groups homes, a market, guesthouse, kitchen gardens, menders and a field registry within a compact neighborhood. Goods can be traded in marks at agreed prices. Food comes from cultivated beds, mushrooms, managed pollination, lake produce and imports. Freight returns with fragrances, seeds, fibers, optical shell and carefully documented materials. Stable supplies and quiet ordinary lives exist alongside adventurous work.

Household traditions mark first blooms, returning carriers and remembered ancestors. Some residents treat island buoyancy as sacred, others study it; there is no compulsory deity or universal fae worldview. Language follows the speaker’s actual knowledge. Local personal names follow the established First name Last name preference; Elvish remains represented as French.

Asterveil Fieldwork and Permissions.text:
The field registry in Asterveil Canopy matches visitors with finite work: ecology counts, weather surveys, route assessment, equipment recovery, material procurement, predator problems and investigation of unusual readings. Bellwind Conservatory receives research results; crossing crews handle transport and safety work. A duty-holder is a role for a generated persistent person, not a new named NPC invented in every conversation.

Local permission states a site, purpose, collection limit and protected conditions. The court’s travel key does not confer ownership of a nest, specimen or ruin. Ordinary observation from public approaches needs no elaborate bureaucracy. Destructive sampling, taking cultivated stock or entering a protected working site needs an actual agreement. Most wild materials are not individual private property, but conservation limits and existing claims still matter.

Any academy can undertake an appropriate approved assignment. Magical combat, engineering, herbology, negotiation, physical fieldcraft and careful record work can all contribute. The four regions do not correspond to four mandatory affinities. A local contract only counts toward the separate authorized academy expedition when its actual agreed court scope, team, field result and debrief satisfy that expedition’s own conditions. Tourism, automatic arrival and an unrelated kill do not confer educational credit.

Asterveil Ecology and Progression.text:
Cloudbloom’s woods and meadows support grazers, small mana beasts and ambush predators. Rimeglass adds cold, altitude, charged mineral perches and concealed conifer hunters. Mirrorwater requires attention to depth, channels, footing and reflective lures. Amethyst’s broken ridges and acoustic terrain favor creatures that hide their outline, redirect sound or exploit open approaches. Dangerous creatures need not be enormous; patience, camouflage and familiar terrain can make a small hunter formidable.

The archipelago’s species have distinct bodies, habits and territories. Peaceful wildlife, wary creatures, sapient communities and hostile monsters share these islands. The outer reaches reward a prepared expedition; the innermost frontier demands experienced companions and a sound retreat route.

Cut reeds, repeated wakes, feeding scars, wing dust and charged mineral perches can reveal what lives nearby. Abandoned equipment may tell a less reassuring story. A cleared nest stays empty until something genuinely takes its place. Retreat, protecting a habitat, collecting with permission and hunting a dangerous beast can lead to different outcomes.

Asterveil Materials and Procurement.text:
Materials have provenance, condition and limited uses. Threadwing scales suit pollen screens; discarded Petalglass shell supports optical studies; discharged Stormglass plates can be examined for charge control; mature glassreed suits filters and fine tubing; Prismfold membrane reveals refractive structure; old calibration components support precision research. These are examples of field value, not automatic recipes or free permanent bonuses.

Obtain an actual sample before inventory changes. Collection requires actual access and recovery; quantity, condition and ownership matter. Shed material, a traded specimen, a permitted cutting and recovered remains have different costs. Active charge, toxins, fragile tissue and storage can matter through real supported effects. Merely being magical does not make a material a health or mana potion.

A report can include a control comparison, a negative result or a reason extraction should not occur. Contract terms determine payment. Prices and payments are reckoned in marks, and a settled fee is not owed a second time. Selling the same specimen removes it; a copied field record is information rather than duplicated physical material.

Asterveil Survey Ruins.text:
Broken Halo Ruins, Drowned Orrery and Stillstar Sanctum preserve different parts of an old practical survey tradition. They measured wind, light, water cycles and instrument alignment; they were not one omnipotent mechanism controlling every island. Dates, affiliations and losses must be established from actual evidence. Similar design does not prove a single war, fallen dynasty or secret villain.

Most failures have local causes: a damaged counterweight, a reflection produced by a living animal, a blocked channel or a resonator deliberately isolated after harming nearby habitat. A party can distinguish those causes through real comparison and inspection. Findings persist and can be reported without creating an automatic grand conspiracy.

Old constructs and rare materials may be dangerous. Permission, stabilization, copying a record and taking an artifact are separate acts. An intact part is not guaranteed after demolition. Preserve a genuine decision to leave an unsafe or important object in place as a possible successful outcome when the commission allows it.

Asterveil Wilderness Expeditions.text:
Expedition scenes begin with a concrete purpose and method: survey a channel, recover a damaged instrument, protect a carrier, collect a bounded sample, identify a predator or investigate a specific anomaly. Use a small manageable cast and existing places. A contract can be exciting without recruiting every acquaintance or inventing another village beyond the map.

Prepare at Cloudbloom, the Rimeglass Refuge, Reedglass Anchorage or Heatherwatch Shelf. Actual kit, permission, field knowledge and companions create different approaches. Bad preparation has specific visible consequences; it does not make every missing signature a new quest. The shortest safe answer may be to withdraw and return better equipped. A successful finite job is allowed to end.

Local commissions cover work across the regions. Generated contracts may use other existing sites and species, with a clear objective, actual payment terms, a completion event and a persistent outcome. Reported signs and sightings belong to actual places in the archipelago. Quiet camps and settlement scenes remain possible between fieldwork.

Asterveil Crossing Cooperative.text: Carrier crews, landing workers and maintenance specialists operate attended crossings between the settlement and the three regional approaches. They maintain short spans where appropriate, sail carriers, landing harnesses, weather instruments and rescue stores. Routes link Cloudbloom Landing, Tetherroot Chain, Rimeglass Refuge, Reedglass Anchorage and Heatherwatch Shelf. A passenger buys or joins an actual service; membership does not issue a court portal key.

Bellwind Field Circle.text: A small association of local researchers, habitat keepers and field registrars works through Bellwind Conservatory and the Canopy registry. It compares observations, records species and materials, and arranges bounded research commissions. It is not a fifth academy, a universal adventurers’ guild or a rival government. Outsiders can collaborate without joining.

The Silken Descent.text:
A compact cave complex repurposed by Vhalessra and the Silken Brood. Its four major chambers descend in order from Silken Portal Room through Threadfall Galleries and Sunken Broodworks to Widow’s Crucible. Old cargo tracks, bronze winding gear and carved load patterns survive beneath newer living silk. In the cold galleries, shed shells and strand vibrations expose a territorial predator’s habits. Below, warm mineral water and tension machinery feed the matron’s experimental web-anchor. Her attempt to extend a route beyond the chasm snagged an Evertree transit passage; it did not reveal an ancient prophecy or prove that the Evertree is failing. The apparatus and its strain damage support an investigation rather than explaining the whole wider world.

The ascent remains physically connected. The stable entrance home arch is separate from her experimental anchor and remains usable before and after the confrontation. Defeating every creature is unnecessary. A viable traversed route, displaced defender or genuine agreement can matter as much as a kill. Established crossings and resolved defenders stay resolved on return; leaving does not refill an untouched cache or respawn an enemy. Ordinary samples and salvaged tools need actual recovery; the shattered web-anchor leaves a distinctive silver-black trophy.

The upper gallery has three hunting groups; the broodworks has a coordinated arachne span guard, a winch nest and two gatekeepers. Vhalessra is a fixed level-45 boss, defended by Kharvess and Orrhask. Finding this place at level twenty invites investigation; it does not make its deepest fight safe for an unprepared solo traveler. The party may withdraw, recruit actual willing companions, prepare or return stronger. These are finite defenders, not an endlessly regenerating trial.

Silken Descent Routes and Map Scale.text:
The two region tiles are one close vertical cutaway: Silken Chasm above Silken Depths. They show rooms and passages within a small dungeon, not a hundred-kilometre march. The canonical distances are short stairs and galleries, a few minutes per cleared connection; fighting, cautious survey and a specific obstacle determine the elapsed time. Voyage uses the world’s shared region grid for pin placement; coordinate travel-distance labels on this diagram are not literal underground kilometres. Do not change the scale of Glowhaven or the other realms.

The only main route is Portal Chamber → First Chamber (Threadfall Galleries) → Second Chamber (Sunken Broodworks) → Boss Chamber (Widow’s Crucible). Side routes are areas within those chambers. A map selection expresses a destination; it cannot pass an unresolved connecting obstacle or create a room inside solid rock. Earn the gallery route and broodworks gate through actual resolved methods. Once opened they stay open. Backtracking through reached rooms and returning home do not require solving them again. The navigation guard retains the last valid chamber on an attempted skip; narrate that actual state rather than the requested destination. A future change that removes a passage must be a real new event, not automatic difficulty inflation.

Dungeon Enemy Groups.text:
The Silken Descent is inhabited territory. Giant spiders wait near feeding grounds and webbed approaches, while arachne defenders exploit narrow passages, bindings and sheltered firing positions. Several defenders may cooperate: one holds an approach while another circles, binds or strikes from cover.

The deeper chambers show increasing organization. Fresh strands, disturbed dust, wrapped remains and movement above the light can betray an occupied passage. Refuge floors and defensible thresholds offer places to pause, but a quiet corridor is no promise that the next chamber is empty.

Vhalessra holds the lowest chamber with Kharvess and Orrhask. Their defenses protect her control of the web-anchor, not an endless reserve of soldiers. Fallen defenders and broken defenses leave lasting gaps. Careful movement, disabling an approach, forcing a withdrawal or securing a genuine surrender may change the descent without requiring every creature to die. Returning travelers encounter the consequences of what happened before.

Adventurer's Guild.text:
The Adventurer's Guild is an international organization with a court-permitted branch in Glowhaven. It connects clients with registered adventurers for deliveries, escorts, monster control, surveys, recovery and other agreed work. Martial adventurers, mages and mixed parties can join; academy faculty and the academies themselves may post requests without controlling the guild. It is a professional association, not an academy, police force or government.

Applicants must pass the adventurer licensure exam before receiving a Bronze badge. The ladder is Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum. The badge held is the mechanical credential for the jobs a character may accept; higher ranks may accept lower-tier work. Promotions are offered after a sufficient record of completed guild work and require a genuinely completed assessment and the candidate's acceptance. Power or fame alone does not silently change a badge.

Komugi Hanabishi handles reception, registration and records at the Glowhaven branch. Jobs have a stated scope, badge requirement and reward. The posted reward is the amount paid to the adventurer. Accepting a contract does not grant access to private property, foreign restricted sites or a portal. Court-issued portal keys are separate permissions obtained from the Sage's Court.

Court Administration and Justice.text: Sae Takasago oversees delegated petition and passage administration, while Tadashi Morishige reviews public-works expenditure and actual workmanship. Court permission and a genuine key issue remain necessary for portal access. At the Magistrate’s Hall, Tomoe Hoshizaki hears cases and Ryōichi Naruse practices as an independent defense attorney. His Phoenix Wing Academy education is part of his background, not a right to bypass court records or decide a verdict. Actual evidence, lawful process and decisions still matter. The principal masked elite operatives are Ayame Kazehara, Gōtarō Iwamine, Shion Kurobane and Seiran Yukitsugu; they serve the existing court-directed force and have individual limits rather than shared omniscience.

Magic Discipline — Arcane.text:
Raw mana shaped into force. Usually the first magical discipline a mage studies, it provides a practical introduction to controlling release, shape and stability.

Scope: Bolts, force impacts, barriers, tethers, platforms, geometric tools and arcane constructs. A construct can have a prepared simple behavior; a separately called familiar or autonomous elemental belongs to Summoning.

Practice and mastery: A novice projects a brief force pulse or supports a small shape. Trained work combines stable surfaces, restraints and precise releases. Advanced work maintains articulated constructs or several coordinated shapes. Mastery can improve deliberate ambient mana uptake by a small amount; it does not create a self-funding spell or an instant full refill.

Boundaries: Arcane is not universal access to every discipline. General invention and theory use Spellcraft. Active regeneration must have its own reviewed technique and cost; ordinary turns supply no passive refill and explicit recovery is applied once.

Approach: Logic. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Fire.text:
Creation and manipulation of flame and heat, including combustion, controlled explosive release and advanced thermal work.

Scope: Ignition, fire streams, shaped flame, heat transfer, thermal gradients and heating actual objects. Heat manipulation can move heat away as well as concentrate it; shaping a lasting ice structure is Ice work.

Practice and mastery: A novice lights and steers a small flame. Trained work produces useful jets, screens and deliberate bursts. Advanced work controls heat through materials and shapes dangerous releases around chosen routes. Mastery can govern a large thermal field or a major explosive working with the corresponding preparation and Mana.

Boundaries: A dramatic flame is not automatically a hit. Fuel, nearby people and the fate of transferred heat matter. Fire does not conjure a permanent supply of fuel or replace Ice proficiency.

Approach: Passion. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Water.text:
The creation, movement and shaping of liquid water: flow, pressure, currents and wet terrain.

Scope: Jets, lashes, water screens, carried streams, buoyancy assistance, pumping and directing an existing body of water. Conjured water supports a temporary working.

Practice and mastery: A novice gathers or shifts a small quantity. Trained work directs pressure and changes a local flow. Advanced work divides currents, supports moving barriers or controls a larger watercourse. Mastery can sustain major hydraulic works with an actual source, scale and burden.

Boundaries: Water does not include Ice, blood control or extracting bodily fluids. Neither a water motif nor cleaning a wound supplies Healing. Temporary conjuration does not become permanent drinking supplies.

Approach: Passion. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Earth.text:
The shaping and movement of earth, stone, soil, clay and sand.

Scope: Raised cover, trenches, shaped footing, moving sand, compacted structures, stone projectiles and the controlled alteration of actual terrain.

Practice and mastery: A novice shifts loose earth or shapes a small surface. Trained work raises useful cover and disrupts footing. Advanced work handles layers, supporting structures and moving granular fields. Mastery can undertake large earthworks without making their weight, stability or surroundings irrelevant.

Boundaries: Earth includes sand, but precise metal control belongs to Metal. Altering real terrain can persist; conjured stone is temporary spell matter, not free permanent construction stock.

Approach: Passion. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Wind.text:
The shaping of air, pressure and currents, from delicate ventilation to violent directed flow.

Scope: Gusts, pressure strikes, redirected air, ventilation, assisted movement and work on clouds and local weather where the conditions support it.

Practice and mastery: A novice stirs or guides a small current. Trained work creates coherent gusts and useful pressure changes. Advanced work manages sustained moving flows and limited cloud or weather intervention. Master-level techniques can support controlled flight; basic wind assistance is not sustained flight.

Boundaries: Weather depends on an actual atmosphere, scale and developing conditions. Sound is a distinct vibration discipline, and Lightning is not granted by pointing at a cloud.

Approach: Passion. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Lightning.text:
The generation and direction of electrical discharge and the control of useful electrical effects.

Scope: Arcs, charged contact, directed bolts, electrical conduction and disciplined storm-related discharge. Electrical effects on a device still require understanding the device.

Practice and mastery: A novice produces a controlled spark. Trained work directs a reliable discharge or timed contact release. Advanced work shapes branching paths, charged zones or storm-fed attacks. Mastery can handle great electrical power with exact paths and real collateral risks.

Boundaries: Conductivity and insulation influence the attempt. Lightning does not automatically paralyze every target, confer Wind weather control or give bodily super-speed; deliberate bodily enhancement is Enchantment.

Approach: Passion. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Ice.text:
A discipline historically derived from Water, now studied independently. It governs freezing, frost, ice structures and precise low-temperature work.

Scope: Ice weapons, barriers, frozen surfaces, cold transfer, preservation and the thermal conditions around a freezing working.

Practice and mastery: A novice lays frost or forms a small piece. Trained work makes coherent ice tools and controlled slippery terrain. Advanced work builds strong structures or manages a field of cold. Mastery can sustain intricate frozen architecture or a large cold working.

Boundaries: Water study is not a prerequisite. Fire also studies heat transfer, but does not thereby shape ice. Freezing a resisting creature is a contested attack. Conjured ice fades with its working; genuinely frozen existing water follows ordinary thawing afterward.

Approach: Intuition. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Light.text:
The creation and direction of illumination and concentrated light, including starlight techniques and tightly focused beams.

Scope: Lighting, signals, glare, reflected or refracted paths, luminous screens, star-like projectiles and laser-like attacks.

Practice and mastery: A novice illuminates or signals. Trained work directs a beam, creates a sharp flash or controls useful reflected light. Advanced work coordinates several rays or sustained optical effects. Mastery supports spectacular starlight fields and highly concentrated beams.

Boundaries: Light is not Healing and does not automatically purify a soul, reveal every secret or punish undead. Starlight is an expression of this discipline, not permission to move stars, manipulate gravity or predict the future.

Approach: Empathy. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Metal.text:
A discipline historically derived from Earth, now studied independently. It governs metallic matter, from bending existing metal to sophisticated mineral and structural work.

Scope: Bending, reshaping, reinforcing, joining and moving metal. Advanced-to-master work includes difficult transmutation of metallic minerals and the conjuration of solid metallic spell matter.

Practice and mastery: A novice flexes a small suitable piece. Trained work shapes functional edges, catches or reinforcement. Advanced work manages articulated metal and controlled mineral conversion. Mastery can undertake demanding metallic transmutation or maintain large, precise conjured structures.

Boundaries: Earth is not a prerequisite. Existing material altered or processed can remain changed. Conjured metal is temporary and cannot be sold as enduring bullion or substituted for permanent crafting components. Transmutation is not unrestricted conversion of living flesh into gold.

Approach: Logic. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Nature.text:
Magic of plants and botanical life, including the creation of temporary plant matter and the growth or repair of actual plants.

Scope: Roots, vines, thorns, seeds, leaves, botanical structures and plant health. It can coax real growth where the plant and conditions permit.

Practice and mastery: A novice encourages a small growth or shapes a simple botanical effect. Trained work makes controlled tangles, thorn weapons and living cover. Advanced work coordinates larger growths or repairs damaged vegetation. Mastery can manage elaborate botanical terrain and difficult plant recovery.

Boundaries: Nature cannot heal non-plant creatures or command every animal. Conjured thorns or plant matter fade; real growth still needs viable matter and conditions and is not an unlimited instant food factory.

Approach: Empathy. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Sound.text:
A demanding, niche discipline historically derived from Wind, now studied independently. It concerns vibration, resonance and the transmission or suppression of sound.

Scope: Tuned pressure pulses, resonant impacts, dampening, projected voices, vibration sensing and the study of how structures respond to frequency.

Practice and mastery: A novice shapes a tone or hushes a small noise. Trained work projects a precise pulse or useful local silence. Advanced work finds and exploits a particular resonance. Mastery can coordinate a complex vibration field or an exceptionally focused sonic release.

Boundaries: Wind is not a prerequisite. Sound is often less convenient than a direct elemental spell and rewards technical precision. Silence is not universal anti-magic: many prepared blueprints use no spoken incantation.

Approach: Intuition. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Gravity.text:
The alteration of local pull, effective weight and the direction in which a burden falls.

Scope: Levitation, load assistance, weighted zones, pulls, assisted leaps, controlled descent and pressure against a resisting target.

Practice and mastery: A novice lightens a small burden. Trained work lifts objects or changes a limited vector. Advanced work coordinates moving loads and contested local fields. Mastery can sustain strong, broad or highly selective gravitational effects.

Boundaries: A resisted field is not an automatic crush. Gravity does not itself fold distance or change time. It is the foundational study required before Space.

Approach: Logic. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Space.text:
A difficult advanced development of Gravity that bends spatial relationships. Serious study requires established Gravity proficiency rather than merely a Space affinity.

Scope: Short spatial displacements, geometric distortion, tears, bounded spatial barriers and prepared portals or teleportation. Later mastery can bridge long distances.

Practice and mastery: The initial study benchmark is Gravity Magic 25. Early Space work handles tiny distortions and very short moves to clearly perceived safe points. Trained and advanced techniques extend precision, carried mass and tactical reach. Master-level travel can reach a genuinely learned distant destination with the necessary preparation, Mana and actual route resolution.

Boundaries: Private teleportation is possible; court keys regulate the public portal network, not ownership of all spatial knowledge. A journey requires a real successful passage and a safe arrival at its intended destination. A map label is not proof of a learned destination. Space does not create new realms or grant every dungeon route, move or carry unwilling targets without resistance, or alter time.

Approach: Logic. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Void.text:
Magic of absence, shadows, suppression and disruption: a difficult counterpart to making an effect present.

Scope: Local darkness, shadow shaping, gaps in an active working, counterspell attempts, suppression and trained destructive void techniques.

Practice and mastery: A novice makes a small shadow or interference. Trained work disrupts a specific weak point in a spell or projects a bounded void attack. Advanced work suppresses a defined active effect or shapes a selective absence. Mastery can contest formidable magic with equivalent knowledge, timing and commitment.

Boundaries: Void is not universal cancellation, automatic erasure or ordinary Space teleportation. It does not extract another humanoid’s protected internal mana. Targets and opposing spells resist; a rare affinity does not supply the missing technique.

Approach: Intuition. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Healing.text:
Restorative magic for living creatures: treating injury, supporting repair and addressing conditions within the caster’s actual medical knowledge.

Scope: Closing fresh wounds, stabilizing injury, supporting recovery and more demanding treatment where the specific working and condition permit it.

Practice and mastery: A novice assists a small fresh injury. Trained work handles useful acute restoration. Advanced work can manage difficult wounds or particular conditions with appropriate knowledge. Mastery supports extraordinary restoration without making every permanent injury, disease or consequence trivially reversible.

Boundaries: Healing is not Light, Nature plant-work or Soul spirit-work. It does not automatically reverse age, resurrect the dead, refill Mana or Stamina, or remove established soul shock. Apply the actual treatment once and follow the existing restoration bands when no more specific result exists.

Approach: Empathy. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Enchantment.text:
The deliberate magical alteration of objects or bodies, including learned strength, speed, resilience and other functional enhancements.

Scope: Temporary imbuements, tuned properties, conditional effects and trained bodily augmentation. Durable work can need suitable materials and a prepared installation.

Practice and mastery: A novice sustains one modest alteration. Trained work gives a purposeful, repeatable enhancement. Advanced work handles demanding bodily techniques or complex prepared properties. Mastery can achieve extremely powerful enhancement through actual training, expense and control.

Boundaries: Circulating mana alone is not automatic augmentation. Enchantment does not compel love, repair every injury or design an integrated machine by itself. Magitech handles magical-mechanical construction; the relevant physical skill still delivers an enhanced strike.

Approach: Logic. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Summoning.text:
Calling, forming and directing familiars, summoned constructs, elementals and other specific entities through learned bonds or prepared methods.

Scope: Temporary helpers, called companions, prepared elemental bodies and coordinated summoned assistance. Different techniques establish different identities, autonomy, duration and costs.

Practice and mastery: A novice forms or calls a small helper. Trained work maintains one useful familiar or temporary entity. Advanced work coordinates specialized entities or several bounded roles. Mastery can sustain impressive summons without turning one cast into unlimited independent actions.

Boundaries: Arcane can shape directed force constructs; Summoning develops the entity, bond and behavior. A summoned ally or pet is distinct from an independent person; traveling together requires an actual arrangement. An actual summoned attacker needs its own supported identity and resolved action; no duplicate automatic hit accompanies the summoning.

Approach: Empathy. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Illusion.text:
The construction of misleading sensory appearances, impressions and decoys.

Scope: Visual and other learned sensory effects, disguising an appearance, false routes, projected doubles and perceptual misdirection.

Practice and mastery: A novice changes a simple appearance. Trained work maintains a useful convincing decoy. Advanced work coordinates several senses or makes an illusion respond within its design. Mastery can stage elaborate, coherent sensory scenes.

Boundaries: An illusion has no physical substance unless another working supplies it. It changes appearances, not recorded grades, ownership or the underlying place. Attentive observation, contradictory evidence and the actual observer matter.

Approach: Intuition. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Divination.text:
The oracle’s discipline: perceiving signs, distant or hidden impressions, traces of the past and possible futures.

Scope: Focused questions, readings, omens, magical investigation, retrospective impressions and prospective warnings.

Practice and mastery: A novice finds a relevant impression in an accessible sign. Trained work answers a bounded question with useful evidence or uncertainty. Advanced work reads a more difficult trace or a branching possibility. Mastery can perceive profound past or future patterns while distinguishing them from guaranteed outcomes.

Boundaries: Divination observes rather than outwardly manipulates time. Oracles receive no Time affinity or automatic Time proficiency. Readings do not establish universal omniscience, another person’s consent or legal proof without evidence.

Approach: Intuition. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Soul.text:
Magic concerning spirits and the boundary between life and death, including exorcism, possession, spiritual wards, necromancy and raising undead.

Scope: Spirit perception, contact, protection, contested binding or release, spiritual injury and specific necromantic animations. The actual spell must distinguish a corpse animated by magic from a working involving a conscious spirit.

Practice and mastery: A novice perceives a limited spiritual sign or attempts a simple ward. Trained work can settle or repel a minor presence and learn a bounded animation. Advanced work handles difficult exorcism, particular undead or a demanding spiritual bond. Mastery can confront great spiritual forces through a defined working.

Boundaries: Necromancy is decided spell by spell: identify the remains, whether a conscious soul is involved, its agency or resistance, control burden and duration. Undead do not universally contain a person’s soul. Raising remains is not resurrection of the original living person. Ordinary Soul study does not establish fatal humanoid mana extraction, guaranteed possession or routine resurrection.

Approach: Empathy. This describes magical execution, not a required personality or morality. An affinity eases study; it does not grant spells or mastery. Casting a learned spell uses this discipline. Designing a new spell or substantially changing its blueprint uses spellcraft.

Magic Discipline — Time.text:
Time is an exceptionally difficult development of Space concerned with temporal relationships. Divination observes possible futures or traces of the past; Time attempts to alter temporal conditions themselves.

There is no natural Time affinity. Even oracles must approach it through exceptional study rather than an awakening or inherited gift. Local acceleration, delay and temporal anchoring belong to tightly bounded advanced workings. Real mastery requires a deep command of Space, precise spell design and an extraordinary source of instruction or a genuine breakthrough. Ordinary schools do not teach it, and public spellbooks do not supply a convenient route to mastery.

A powerful temporal working has consequences and limits. It does not casually undo a death, erase a completed undertaking, restore spent resources or rewrite another person’s choices. No temporal ability is assumed merely because a caster names one.

Spellcraft and Personal Spell Invention.text:
Spellcraft is the shared craft of understanding and designing spell blueprints. It covers magical theory, reading mana traces, diagnosing a working, and inventing or substantially modifying a spell. Every player begins with this foundational skill; possessing it does not make someone a trained caster.

A new spell design MUST use an actual spellcraft check. First establish the intended effect, discipline, scope and available knowledge. A simple familiar-scale experiment can be attempted in one scene; a difficult design needs appropriate research, testing, tools or instruction. A real result can produce a reproducible blueprint or a useful correction. Naming a spell is not making it.

Casting an already learned spell uses its discipline, not a compulsory second Spellcraft check. Learning a teacher’s existing blueprint is distinct from inventing one. Ordinary physical techniques require their own training, not Spellcraft. Knowledge from another discipline is not granted by a successful design roll. Personalized notation, body casting and optional words or gestures are ordinary; successful invention is not automatically rare real-time Freeform casting.

Common spell libraries and personally invented blueprints coexist. Established named spells are recognizable techniques; they do not exhaust what a trained discipline can attempt. A personal spell needs a reproducible function, not an evolutionary replacement chain. A mage can call a familiar working by a personal name without creating another mechanical card.

Conjuration and Lasting Materials.text: Conjured water, ice, plants, stone and metal are temporary spell matter and fade when their working ends. Actual material moved, shaped, cooled, grown or transmuted can remain changed, subject to its real properties and conditions. Temporary conjuration is useful for combat and practical work, but is not permanent bullion, food, drinking supplies or manufacturing stock. A genuine thermal change, extinguished fire or cut already suffered is not retroactively undone when the conjured medium fades. Real plant growth needs viable matter and conditions; metallic transmutation works on suitable actual matter through a demanding process.

Magitech and Enchantment.text:
Designing, building, fitting, inspecting, maintaining and repairing magical equipment and integrated magical-mechanical systems. This single skill combines the former Artifice scope with mana circuits, power routing, regulators, mechanisms, device safety, practical foci and engineered tools.

A novice inspects a simple fitting or circuit. Trained work assembles or repairs reliable equipment from a suitable design and parts. Advanced work diagnoses linked systems, develops controlled devices and reverse-engineers unfamiliar machinery with real investigation. Mastery supports complex original machines and demanding field repairs.

A mundane mechanism needs no new spell. A newly invented spell powering a device also requires Spellcraft; applying an existing spell to equipment can involve the relevant learned discipline. Use one primary check for the actual stage rather than automatically rolling every related skill. Magitech supplies neither materials nor an external mana battery by default. A prepared device fires through its actual operating method; engineering knowledge is not universal weapon proficiency. A customer’s item remains theirs.

Magitech is a learned technical skill, not a natural magical affinity. Enchantment changes a property; Magitech designs and constructs the integrated device. Spellcraft invents a new magical operation. One project may have distinct stages without every use requiring three simultaneous accuracy rolls.

Health, Mana and Stamina.text: Health measures bodily harm, Mana is usable spellcasting capacity, and Stamina is physical exertion. Ordinary weapon attacks, routine defense and ordinary travel remain useful without spending either casting Mana or a technique’s Stamina. Demanding physical techniques use Stamina; spells use Mana; an explicitly mixed demanding technique can use both. Spending one does not automatically damage the others. Zero Stamina leaves careful movement and ordinary action available; zero usable Mana leaves a living person conscious. Resource settings define costs and recovery. Stamina is not an Endurance attribute and does not create a new personality requirement.

Drakenspire — Households Across the Riva.text:
The great clans contain people with different ambitions. Tsubaki Iwatsugu prefers durable administration, while Shūhei Iwatsugu wants field independence. Koharu Yukinose and Ryōma Arashimine are publicly betrothed adults from rival households; their engagement is voluntary, and both retain personal agency. Iori Yukinose and Tsugumi Arata have a private adult relationship that neither clan office nor the player can automatically claim to know.

Household and work ties extend beyond the chiefs. Noboru Ōhira and Atsuko Ōhira, Sachie Handa and Eitarō Handa, Daisuke Toyama and Toki Toyama, and Michiru Aonuma and Haruto Aonuma are established married couples. Their work, affection and disagreements continue without a player’s intervention. Not every eligible-looking resident is single, and friendly service is not a romantic commitment.

Drakenspire — Nonhumanoid Names.text: Humanoid residents use the established local personal-name conventions in given-name-first order. Individually named nonhumanoids need not have a human surname. Rovakthuun has an original draconic compound-syllable name; Orrum has a short personal name. Use those exact identities when known, while preserving the difference between a familiar local epithet, an uncertain sighting and a true name learned in play. They are original world characters, not crossover figures or asserted translations from another setting.

Drakenspire — Orrum and the White Silenc.text:
Orrum is a particular isolated yeti, a rare giant of the remote snow country. He has dense white fur, a blunt nonhuman face, small blue eyes, huge careful hands and enough intelligence for preferences, gestures and a limited spoken vocabulary. He carries a weathered branch and keeps a few small objects. He is not a generic respawning boss or a tame animal.

People in the city usually know doubtful tracks and stories. Haruto Aonuma once found a lost bundle moved away from dangerous ice but has no proof of its helper and does not know Orrum’s name or shelter. A visit to the White Silence does not guarantee contact. Ordinary giants remain reusable npcTypes elsewhere; do not generate interchangeable yeti under a separate type.

Orrum prefers withdrawal and may defend himself decisively when trapped. His caution is not default murderous hostility. Investigation, patient conduct and respect for an escape route can matter. His home is not publicly known, and asking about him does not guarantee a meeting.

Drakenspire — Succession and Public Busi.text:
Daizen Iwatsugu holds both the elected Jarlship and the Iwatsugu chiefship. Neither office automatically passes to one child or relative. Ryōma Arashimine is acknowledged as a household heir, not as heir to the Jarlship. A clan endorsement, personal promise, public reputation or marriage can influence an election without substituting for it.

The Jarl coordinates shared defense, national commitments and matters crossing clan boundaries. The Clan Assembly debates shared obligations and records decisions through Noboru Ōhira. Setsuna Takigawa hears ordinary cases at the Hold’s Judgment House; gate officers and Gōki Shishido’s guard enforce actual law within their responsibilities. A chief cannot convert household dissatisfaction into a national arrest order.

Public petitions, evidence and costs matter. The government has ordinary business as well as rivalry: repairs, disputed cargo, staffing, winter stores, public observances and access requests. Private conversations do not automatically become public law or completed actions.

Drakenspire — Work, Reputation and Prese.text:
Advanced metalwork and raw magical resources connect independent workers with clan contracts. Benjirō Kanemori’s respected spellblade workshop, Chisato Higuruma’s foundry floor, Isamu Murakoshi’s mine crew, Madara Senzaki’s amber surveys and Takumi Hasebe’s assay work have distinct functions. Saeha Kogetsu brokers resource trade without owning every producer. Their disagreements concern workmanship, pay, promised access and practical risk as well as prestige.

Akitsu Arashimine’s channel assembly has drawn disputed test findings. Tsubaki Iwatsugu faces repair costs and contractor demands. Masatsugu Yukinose uses private credit and commitments to build political leverage. These are separate situations rather than one conspiracy explaining every shop. A performer’s premiere, a household workshop or an honest day’s fieldwork can matter without joining the succession struggle.

Phoenix Wing Academy — Academic Occasion.text:
Phoenix Wing Academy follows the four-year adult program while students build their own studies, friendships and outside lives. The major course occasions include original spell design, a joint familiar practical, a shared festival, genuine foreign fieldwork, one substantial practical capstone and a closing celebration. These occur through actual progress and invitations; they do not replace ordinary classes or require a whole cohort to travel together. A capstone is a significant chosen investigation or experiment, not a recurring annual paperwork exercise.

Local opportunities: The Line Behind You: A team arena challenge rewards keeping a partner in play, while Takeru Akabane wants a spectacular solo finish. The Prize in the Flask: Ranka Kagari has announced a potion contest with a small prize and hopes someone produces a formula she can sell. A Demonstration of Terrible Importance: Yūma Kurobane wants his allegedly world-shaking demonstration on the student program; the spell itself is decidedly modest.
