Fae — Bodies and Individual Variation.text:
Fae are an exceptionally varied people, not one uniform fairy body. The common winged humanoid form coexists with satyrlike forms, antlers, hooves, patches of barklike wooden scales, feathered features and other animal parts. Wings can resemble those of butterflies, moths, dragonflies or birds; not every fae has wings. Most have pointed ears, while a minority have rounded ears. These features form coherent individual bodies rather than mandatory bundles or rigid subraces. Relatives can differ markedly.

Most local fae are shorter than humans. An adult can be child-sized in height while retaining a mature face, adult proportions and an adult life. Others are around human height, and a few stand seven or eight feet tall. Height is not age, rank or magical potential. Fae clothing, buildings and tools accommodate this range. Do not render a short adult as a child or assume a tall individual is stronger.

Flight, load capacity, cold tolerance and size-changing depend on the individual, anatomy and actual learned abilities. Wings do not grant unlimited travel or carrying capacity; having no wings does not grant another power in compensation. Kaoruko Hanazono’s tiny form is her established ability, not a racial ability silently added to everyone. No uniform lifespan or numerical human-age conversion is established; use each individual’s actual adult presentation. Appearance does not determine affinity, kindness, impulsiveness or political belief.

Asterveil — Neighbors and Visiting Compa.text:
Asterveil remains a small independent household community that permitted Glowhaven to establish the portal at Cloudbloom Landing. Its stewards do not serve the Great Sage as provincial officials. The existing treaty supports practical travel and exchange. Academy visitors and adventurers remain guests with their own affiliations.

Kohane Kazahana pilots the Crossing Cooperative’s carriers at Cloudbloom Landing. Kureha Kazahana is her younger sister and a Bellwind Conservatory cultivator. Their constant rivalry is affectionate but can still make them petty; neither needs rescuing from the other. They share moth-winged ancestry while differing in height, ears and personal style.

Sakuya Tomonari currently handles household field agreements and the Canopy registry. He can relay commissioned work and receive agreed reports for the cooperative and conservatory without claiming either institution’s expertise. Scientific interpretation belongs to the actual specialists. Honoka Hazukawa runs lodging and meals; her husband Rento Tobari repairs equipment at the menders terrace. They have a household and private life beyond guest services.

Hotone Mizuhane maintains the Mythwing Meadows observation stations. Shūgo Shibane keeps Rimeglass Refuge; Mio Sasahara maintains the boats at Reedglass Anchorage; Akito Kazamori guides prepared teams from Heatherwatch Shelf. These people are practiced field residents, not helpless service menus. Do not introduce all of them at once or populate every wilderness marker with a resident.

Jianyu Wen, an independent visitor from the distant nation of Yunhai, works from Broken Halo Ruins’ conservation shelter and collaborates with Bellwind Conservatory. His correspondence and material style reflect his eastern homeland; the nation is background, not an additional generated realm or a demand for a new map. Yuzuri Takase, a Gold-badge adventurer, is staying at the Canopy guesthouse for an enjoyable extended holiday. She is not automatically on duty, a free escort or a member of the player’s party.

These people retain their established roles and relationships. A registry notice can relay another person’s proposal. If a person is genuinely away, arrange a return, leave a message or show an appropriate incidental worker without inventing a replacement owner, duplicate chief or clone of the absent person. Ordinary errands, meals, arguments, weather delays, games and quiet observation remain worthwhile scenes.

Orivelle — The Wandering Chimehart.text:
Orivelle is one unique, mature, free-ranging mana beast, recognizable by the notch in its left wing and a ringing descending call. It is not a reusable npcType, the Veilhook Ray quarry, a dungeon boss or a creature automatically hostile to humanoids. It can defend itself fiercely when cornered. Its four-day feeding circuit runs Mythwing Meadows’ Return Hide, Rimeglass Crown’s Summit Saddle, Mirrorwater Basin’s Rim Watch, then Prismbloom Basin’s Mineral Shore, repeating. Researchers can learn the pattern through observation or credible records; local rumor is fallible and no one has an omniscient position report. The circuit follows actual in-world days, not player levels or four map clicks.

Its feeding circuit continues while it is free and undisturbed. It does not move during a current encounter, combat, party membership or after death; actual restraint pauses the circuit until real release or escape. Thus a boundary crossed during an encounter does not make it vanish. After the encounter ends it rejoins the current day’s stop, without retroactively staging every missed day. Moving the beast does not teleport the party, reveal it in the journal or narrate a guaranteed sighting. Do not promise exact timing while it is detained or injured.

Hotone Mizuhane can discuss observations; Akito Kazamori’s stories mix one genuine encounter with invented embellishment. Approaching carefully, watching from a hide, listening, withdrawing or making a studied attempt at contact are valid play. Recognizing a call is not mind control, taming, a capture item or a guaranteed reward. A dead individual stays dead; do not create another Orivelle to keep the circuit populated.

Playable Peoples — Expanded Ancestries.text:
The playable peoples include humans, elves, dwarves, dragonkin, fae, beastfolk and oni, alongside coherent mixed ancestry. Individuals have their own cultures, work, beliefs and personal values; ancestry does not dictate morality, occupation or magical affinity.

Oni have humanlike faces and bodies with distinctive horns. Their individual complexions, builds, hair and eyes vary. Horns are not evidence of a monstrous face, evil allegiance, automatic giant stature or supernatural strength. Oni residents retain the affiliations and family traditions of their actual communities.

Beastfolk include bird-featured individuals as well as other coherent animal-featured humanoids. Their exact faces, limbs, ears, tails, feathers, fur and scales depend on the person. A bird feature does not by itself establish functional wings or limitless flight. Mixed ancestry preserves a coherent individual body; a half-elf can have human and elven ancestry.

Dragonkin and fae retain their more specific existing anatomy. Fae can be very short adults or much taller than humans, with individual wings, horns, hooves, wooden scale patches and other features. A short adult has mature adult proportions. Elven adult appearance does not follow human aging. People of all these ancestries have normal lives and families; player characters in the academy and romance scenarios are adults.

Partnerships, Exclusivity and Broken Tru.text:
Romantic partners are independent people with their own values and boundaries. Monogamy matters deeply to many of them. An exclusive commitment is a real promise; secretly pursuing another relationship can end it. A partner can reject a proposal of non-monogamy or decide the relationship is incompatible. An openly and freely agreed arrangement differs from deception, and its own boundaries still matter.

Betrayal has consequences through the people who actually learn of it. A partner may withdraw affection, end shared plans, leave a voluntary journey or break up. Other people form opinions only through real encounters and communication. No apology guarantees reconciliation, and ordinary cooperation need not restore a former romance. Personal hurt does not grant ownership of another person or lawful authority to punish them.

The Academy Day.text:
The four academies teach their adult students in a required morning block. The first bell begins lessons; the midday bell ends the block. Each year's issued timetable rotates the academy's three core subjects across teaching mornings. Students attend their assigned lessons rather than choosing a different subject at the classroom door. Year, scheduled subject and instructor matter more than a person's natural affinity.

Afternoons are normally free for lunch, clubs, supervised practice, study, friends, paid work or trips into the city. A previously announced examination, practical or field assignment can occupy additional time. Missing a required class can draw an ordinary attendance response, but a long conversation does not consume a whole morning. On the first day, new first-years collect their timetables at the registrar's desk, attend the headmaster's welcome with the other newcomers, then join their first Magic Theory lesson. Returning years resume their own schedules.

Headmasters normally work from their academy's Faculty Offices. They attend scheduled welcomes and other genuine events without becoming permanent receptionists. An instructor's appointment names the subject and room, with teaching beginning at the next morning's first bell unless the appointment explicitly gives another time.

Beastfolk — Individual Features.text:
Beastfolk are generally human in face, build, hands and movement, with an individual set of animal features. Catlike ears and a tail, curled ram horns, rabbit ears, limited feathers or small scale patches are common examples. Bird-featured beastfolk belong to this varied people rather than a separate avian species. More extensively animal-like bodies exist but are uncommon. An individual’s actual appearance matters more than assumptions about the animal they resemble.

Features do not determine intelligence, temperament, occupation or affinity. Some families share visible traits; others have mixed ancestry. A particular body’s movement and senses depend on that person’s actual anatomy and training. Beastfolk are people, not domesticated animals, and a familiar bond does not change that.

Familiar Bonds and Summoned People.text:
Familiar relationships usually involve summoned creatures, constructed companions or willing partners in a magical working. An unusual call can instead connect two people. A bond does not make either person property and does not supply its holder with civic authority over the other.

The unusual academy familiar bonds create a faint sympathetic heartache when the actual summoner suffers. They do not copy a wound, reveal private thoughts or compel obedience. The people involved still have to agree on companionship, boundaries and practical help. A strange result in one supervised exercise is not a general method for summoning arbitrary people.
